This single experiment simultaneously probes (a) multimodal vs. single-modality benefit, (b) multiprofile + transformer aggregation vs. simpler alternatives, and (c) a lightweight RNA encoder as a floor for later comparisons with scgpt/scvi_n200. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can exploit by upgrading encoders (ViT-L, scgpt); if it underperforms, it signals that the multiprofile/transformer axis or the multimodal combination needs rethinking. Expected relative cost: moderate (~50-60% of the most expensive configs using ViT-L + scgpt + transformer), since resnet50 and pca_n2000 are lightweight, though the transformer aggregation over multiple profiles adds some overhead.

The only completed experiment (config_003, acc=0.573) uses a simple linear PCA (pca_n2000) as the RNA encoder within a multimodal multiprofile transformer-aggregation pipeline. With just one data point, the most informative next step is to test whether upgrading the RNA representation to a learned encoder (scgpt) improves accuracy while holding all other variables constant (multimodal, multiprofile, resnet50, transformer, weighted fusion). This directly probes whether the RNA encoder is the current bottleneck: if scgpt yields a meaningful accuracy gain, it validates investing in richer encoders for subsequent experiments; if not, it redirects attention to the image encoder or aggregation strategy. Expected relative cost: scgpt adds moderate overhead over the near-free PCA, so I estimate roughly 1.4–1.7× the 6.61 GPU hours of config_003 (≈9–11 GPU hours). This is a reasonable exploitation step given 8 experiments remain and the total budget allows a few such mid-cost experiments before needing to consolidate.

Evidence: config_003 (pca_n2000, resnet50, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.573 accuracy at 6.61 GPU hrs, clearly outperforming config_002 (scgpt variant) at 0.494. This establishes pca_n2000 + transformer + multiprofile as a strong baseline. Uncertainty: the fusion strategy (weighted vs concat) has not been tested against the current best; it is a fundamental design choice affecting how RNA and image features are combined. This experiment (config_006) is a single-variable A/B test against config_003, changing only fusion from weighted to concat while keeping all other settings identical. It will clarify whether a more expressive fusion (concat + learned combination) can outperform the simpler weighted sum. Rationale: with 7 experiments remaining, a cheap (~6–7 GPU hrs, similar to config_003) targeted test reduces uncertainty about an important architectural axis at minimal cost, and the result will guide whether to invest remaining budget in concat-based or weighted-based multimodal configurations.

Evidence: pca_n2000 clearly outperforms scgpt (0.579/0.573 vs 0.494), and among the two pca_n2000+resnet50+transformer configs, concat fusion (config_006, 0.579) edges out weighted (config_003, 0.573). All three completed experiments used resnet50 as the image encoder, so the impact of a stronger image backbone remains entirely untested. Question: config_042 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) is a clean single-variable swap from the best config (config_006), replacing resnet50 with the much larger ImageNet-pretrained ViT-Large while holding RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion at their proven-best settings. This directly tests whether a richer image representation can push accuracy above the current ~0.58 ceiling. Rationale: With 6 experiments remaining, identifying whether the image encoder is a bottleneck is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve. If ViT-Large helps, it opens a productive exploitation path (e.g., testing avgpool or scvi_n200 with ViT-Large); if it does not, we can confidently focus on aggregation/fusion/profile-setting variations with resnet50. Expected relative cost: ViT-Large (~300M params) is substantially larger than ResNet50 (~25M params), so I estimate ~10–14 GPU hours versus the ~6.7 for config_006 — roughly 1.5–2× the cost of the current best. This is a justified investment given the potential accuracy gain and the 6 experiments still available.

Evidence: config_042 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved the best accuracy (0.5988) and F1 (0.5777), clearly outperforming resnet50-based configs (~0.573-0.579) and scgpt (0.494). The fusion method is the one remaining untested dimension within this best-performing architecture: concat slightly beat weighted with resnet50 (0.5793 vs 0.5729), but the interaction with the stronger ViT-L encoder is unknown. This experiment (config_047) is a minimal A/B test—identical to config_042 except fusion=weighted—directly clarifying whether weighted fusion could further improve accuracy with the ViT-L encoder. It is the best use of this slot because it exploits the strongest evidence with a single-variable change, has low expected cost (~4-5 GPU hours, similar to config_042's 4.76), and leaves 4 experiments to explore aggregation (avgpool) or profile setting (singleprofile) if needed.

The current best (config_042, acc 0.599) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat. The main remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder can outperform PCA while keeping all other best-performing components fixed. config_048 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat, multiprofile) is a clean single-variable test of the RNA encoder. scgpt was poor (0.494) but with resnet50; scvi_n200 is a lighter, more standard VAE-based encoder that may capture biological structure PCA misses without scgpt's instability. If it matches or beats 0.599, we have a strong new best; if it underperforms, we confirm pca_n2000 as optimal and can focus remaining budget on fusion/aggregation refinements. Expected cost: moderate (~6–8 GPU hrs), since scvi_n200 adds encoder training overhead over PCA but is substantially lighter than scgpt (which added ~5.5 hrs). This is the highest-information experiment given 4 remaining slots: it either opens a new promising direction or locks in the RNA encoder choice so later experiments can target other knobs.

Evidence: config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) achieved a dominant 0.7207 accuracy, far exceeding all other configs (next best: 0.5988). This establishes scvi_n200 as the clear best RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l as the best image encoder. The only untested variant within this top-performing family is the fusion method: config_050 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted). With pca_n2000, concat slightly outperformed weighted (0.5988 vs 0.5856), but the dynamics may differ with the richer scvi_n200 representations. This experiment tests whether weighted fusion could match or exceed concat in the best-performing architecture, directly clarifying the optimal fusion choice. It is the highest-value exploitation step: if weighted matches or beats concat, we find a new best; if not, we confirm config_048 as the optimal configuration and can focus remaining budget on confirming robustness. Expected cost is low (~4.5–4.7 GPU hours, comparable to config_047 and config_048), making it an efficient use of the next slot with 3 experiments remaining.

The evidence strongly points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the optimal modality pair (0.725 accuracy with transformer+weighted, 0.721 with transformer+concat), far outperforming pca_n2000 (~0.60) and scgpt (~0.49). The only untested variation within this winning pair is the aggregation method. config_049 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) directly tests whether the transformer aggregation is necessary for the high accuracy or whether a simpler average-pooling aggregation can match it. This is important because: (1) if avgpool performs comparably (~0.72), we identify a cheaper, simpler architecture for deployment; (2) if avgpool is clearly worse, we confirm transformer aggregation is the critical component and can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning within the transformer family. Expected cost is moderate-to-low (~3–4 GPU hours), comparable to or slightly below the transformer-based configs (3.6–4.7 GPU hours), since avgpool replaces the transformer's self-attention layers. With 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information test that either confirms or challenges the current best configuration's architecture.

Evidence: The best encoder combination (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) has been tested with 3 of 4 aggregation×fusion combinations: transformer+weighted (0.725, config_050), transformer+concat (0.721, config_048), and avgpool+weighted (0.706, config_049). The missing cell is avgpool+concat. This experiment completes the 2×2 grid, confirming that transformer aggregation dominates avgpool regardless of fusion method, and validates config_050 as the robust best. Question tested: Does the aggregation–fusion interaction show any synergy (i.e., could avgpool+concat outperform the other three)? Why this is the best use: It is the lowest-cost, highest-certainty experiment (~4–4.5 GPU hours, similar to config_049's 4.82), it eliminates residual uncertainty about the best architecture, and it frees the final remaining experiment for a more speculative exploration (e.g., singleprofile variants) if the grid confirms config_050's dominance. Expected relative cost: low, comparable to the other scvi_n200+vit_l runs (~4 GPU hours).

Evidence: The top-4 results are all scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile, with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_050, 0.7250) as the best. All four aggregation×fusion combinations for this encoder pair have been tested, so no further gain is expected within that subspace. The remaining untested scvi_n200 + vit_l configurations are the singleprofile variants (config_010, config_027), which remove the aggregation step entirely. Question: This experiment tests whether the multiprofile + transformer architecture is truly necessary or whether a simpler singleprofile pipeline with the same strong encoders (scvi_n200, vit_l) and weighted fusion could be competitive—potentially at lower cost. Rationale: As the final experiment, config_010 is the most logical extension of our best finding (same encoders, same fusion preference), it is the only untested variant in the proven-best encoder space, and it is expected to be relatively cheap (~3–4 GPU hours, no aggregation step) compared to the multiprofile configs. It is very unlikely to beat 0.7250, but it provides the cleanest confirmation that multiprofile + transformer aggregation is the key architectural advantage, and it keeps total GPU hours low. No other untested configuration has a realistic chance of exceeding the current best.

With no prior evidence, the most critical question is whether the full multimodal pipeline with the strongest available encoders and aggregation can achieve high validation accuracy, establishing a performance ceiling for the remaining 9 experiments. config_041 combines scgpt (a purpose-built RNA foundation model, likely superior to PCA or scvi for capturing cell biology), imagenet_vit_l (the most powerful image encoder in the space), transformer aggregation (better than avgpool for modeling inter-profile interactions in multiprofile settings), and weighted fusion (allows adaptive balancing of modalities rather than fixed concatenation). This tests the hypothesis that the best-performing configuration lives in the 'strong encoder + sophisticated aggregation/fusion' region. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can explore whether cheaper components (resnet50, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieve similar accuracy at lower cost. If it underperforms, it localizes the problem to the interaction of these choices rather than a single weak component. Expected relative cost: highest in the search space (scgpt + ViT-L + transformer + multiprofile), but as experiment 1 it is justified to establish the upper bound; 9 experiments remain to explore cheaper alternatives.

Evidence: config_041 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) achieved the best accuracy (0.520) and F1 (0.479) so far, but with only one data point the evidence is sparse. The key uncertainty is whether weighted fusion is optimal or whether concat fusion could yield better accuracy with the same strong encoders and transformer aggregation. This experiment (config_002) changes only the fusion type from weighted to concat, making it a clean single-variable test that directly exploits the most promising architecture while reducing uncertainty about the fusion mechanism. It is the best use of experiment 2 because it builds on the strongest signal we have, is a minimal-risk exploitation step, and will cost approximately the same ~2.8–3.0 GPU hours as config_041 (same multiprofile transformer aggregation with scgpt and imagenet_vit_l encoders), keeping total compute low while gathering critical information to guide the remaining 8 experiments.

The two completed experiments (config_041, config_002) both use scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer, with weighted fusion (0.520) beating concat (0.507). The biggest remaining uncertainty is whether the large imagenet_vit_l backbone is necessary or whether a lighter resnet50 image encoder performs comparably. config_005 (scgpt, resnet50, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable ablation of the image encoder from the current best config. If resnet50 matches or approaches 0.52, it confirms we can save substantial compute for later experiments; if it falls well short, we confirm ViT-L's value and can focus remaining budget on RNA encoder and aggregation variations. Expected relative cost: lower than config_041 (~2.86 GPU hrs) since resnet50 is a much smaller backbone than ViT-L, likely ~1.5–2.0 GPU hrs, making this a cheap and high-information experiment with 7 slots still remaining.

Evidence: The best config so far (config_041, acc=0.520) uses scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. We've confirmed weighted > concat and imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, but the RNA encoder (scgpt) has not been varied. Uncertainty: Whether a lighter VAE-based encoder (scvi_n200) could match or exceed scgpt in the multimodal setting, or whether scgpt's richer pretrained representations are essential. This experiment (config_008) tests scvi_n200 with the same strong image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion, isolating the RNA encoder as the only variable. It is the most informative next step because it clarifies whether the RNA encoder is a bottleneck or whether the image modality dominates. If scvi_n200 performs comparably, it opens cheaper configurations for remaining budget; if scgpt is clearly better, we can focus remaining experiments on other dimensions (aggregation, profile setting). Expected cost: ~2–2.5 GPU hours, slightly below config_041 (2.86) since scvi_n200 is a compact 200-dim VAE rather than the full scGPT transformer, while the expensive imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation remains the same.

Evidence: config_008 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 accuracy, far outperforming all scgpt-based configs (~0.50-0.52), establishing scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer as the dominant architecture. Within that space, only weighted fusion has been tested. Question: Does concat fusion perform comparably or differently when paired with the much stronger scvi_n200 encoder? With scgpt, weighted beat concat by ~1.3 pts (0.520 vs 0.507), but the interaction with a better RNA representation is unknown. This experiment isolates the fusion choice while holding all other (strong) components fixed, reducing uncertainty about whether we can match or exceed 0.725 with a simpler fusion. It is the best next step because it directly exploits the strongest evidence (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer) while probing the one untested dimension, and its expected cost (~3.5-4 GPU hours, similar to config_008's 3.60) keeps total budget manageable with 5 experiments remaining.

The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 as RNA encoder yields ~0.725 accuracy vs ~0.52 for scgpt (a ~20-point gap), making it the clear best encoder. With scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_008) at 0.725, the key remaining uncertainty is whether the image encoder choice (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) still matters significantly when paired with the strong RNA encoder. config_013 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) directly tests this: if resnet50 performs comparably (~0.72), it offers a cheaper alternative for future runs; if it drops substantially, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential and we should focus remaining budget on fine-tuning around the current best. This is the highest-value single experiment because it resolves the most important remaining design axis (image encoder) under the confirmed best RNA encoder, and its expected cost is moderate (resnet50 is a smaller backbone than ViT-L, so likely comparable to or slightly below config_008's 3.6 GPU hours).

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer is clearly the best architecture (config_008: 0.725 acc, 3.60 GPU hrs), and the fusion choice (weighted vs concat) makes negligible difference (0.725 vs 0.721). The remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler avgpool aggregation would perform comparably. This experiment (config_007: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) directly tests that question. If avgpool matches transformer, it offers a meaningfully cheaper configuration for the remaining budget; if it falls short, we confirm transformer's value and can focus remaining experiments on fine-tuning within the transformer family. Expected relative cost: low — avgpool removes the transformer layers, so I estimate ~2–2.5 GPU hours versus 3.60 for the transformer counterpart, making it a cheap, high-information experiment that reduces uncertainty about an important architectural axis before spending the last 3 experiments.

The current best is config_008 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc 0.725, 3.60 GPU-hrs). All four 'best' hyperparameters are already combined there, so marginal gains from further scvi_n200 variants (e.g., concat fusion, resnet50) are unlikely to exceed it. The major untested dimension in the top-performing architecture is the RNA encoder: pca_n2000 has never been paired with the best image encoder + aggregation + fusion. Config_034 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_008. If PCA approaches 0.725, it would offer a cheaper alternative (PCA is a pre-computed linear transform, so no encoder training cost); if it falls well short, it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and the remaining 2 experiments should focus on fine-tuning around the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer core. Expected relative cost: comparable to config_008 (~3–4 GPU-hrs), since the dominant cost is the ViT-L image encoder and transformer aggregation, and the 2000-dim PCA input adds only modest transformer overhead versus the 200-dim scvi latent.

The current best is config_008 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) at 0.725 acc. All multiprofile variants with these encoders have been tested and none exceed it. The key unexplored dimension is whether the multiprofile + transformer aggregation step is actually necessary or whether a simpler singleprofile architecture with the same best encoders (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) and best fusion (weighted) could match or exceed it. Config_031 is the direct singleprofile analog of config_008, removing the aggregation step while keeping all other optimal choices. This tests whether the ~2% gain from transformer aggregation over avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706) is truly additive or whether a cleaner single-profile pipeline avoids overfitting. It is also cheaper (no aggregation layer, estimated ~2–3 GPU hours vs 3.60 for config_008). If it matches or beats 0.725, we gain a cheaper alternative; if it underperforms, it confirms config_008 as the robust optimum and the final experiment can be used to verify or fine-tune around it. This is the highest-information, lowest-cost experiment available given the strong evidence already gathered.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the dominant RNA encoder (0.725 best vs 0.586 for pca, 0.520 for scgpt), multiprofile is essential (0.725 vs 0.537 singleprofile), transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool (+0.019), and imagenet_vit_l slightly edges resnet50 (+0.012). The current best (config_008, 0.7250) already combines all top choices. Among untested configs, config_004 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat, multiprofile) is the highest-expected-accuracy option, as it retains the two strongest factors (scvi_n200, transformer) and only substitutes resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l and concat for weighted. Expected accuracy ~0.71 (extrapolating from config_013 at 0.713 with weighted and config_019 at 0.721 with concat). This is the last experiment; while it is unlikely to surpass 0.7250, it is the most logical exploitation of the scvi_n200+transformer family and tests whether the resnet50+concat combination might produce a synergistic effect. Expected relative cost: moderate, ~5–6 GPU hours (resnet50 adds ~2.5 hrs over ViT-L, concat slightly cheaper than weighted), bringing total to ~49 GPU hours.

With no prior evidence, the highest-priority question is whether the full multimodal + multiprofile architecture with the strongest encoders can achieve high validation accuracy, establishing a performance ceiling for the search. config_005 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) combines the most expressive RNA encoder (scgpt foundation model), the most powerful image encoder (large ViT), the most flexible aggregation (transformer over multiple profiles), and a simple concat fusion. Testing this first gives a strong reference point: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate components to identify which are essential; if it underperforms, we learn that the full architecture is not the right direction and can pivot to cheaper or alternative designs. This is the most expensive configuration in the set (scgpt + ViT-L + transformer aggregation over multiple profiles), but as experiment 1 of 10, establishing the ceiling is the best use of a single slot to guide the remaining 9 experiments efficiently.

The only completed experiment (config_005: multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, ViT-L, transformer, concat) achieved a low accuracy of 0.507 at a high cost of 3.95 GPU hours. With just one data point, the key uncertainty is whether the multiprofile + transformer aggregation architecture is actually contributing or adding complexity that hurts performance. Config_028 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, ViT-L, no aggregation, concat) isolates this question by keeping the same RNA and image encoders while removing the multiprofile/transformer pipeline. If accuracy is similar or better, we identify a simpler, cheaper path and can focus remaining budget on encoder or fusion choices. If it drops, we confirm that multiprofile aggregation is essential and should be retained. Expected relative cost: ~2–2.5 GPU hours (roughly 60% of config_005), since it eliminates the transformer aggregation over multiple profiles. This is the best use of experiment 2 because it reduces the largest architectural uncertainty while staying in the multimodal space and conserving budget for the remaining 8 experiments.

Evidence: config_005 (multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved 0.507 accuracy, substantially outperforming config_028 (singleprofile, same encoders, no aggregation) at 0.435, strongly validating the multiprofile+transformer pipeline. Uncertainty: whether the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted) is a meaningful lever for further improvement in this top-performing architecture. This experiment tests config_010, which is identical to config_005 except fusion changes from concat to weighted—a single-variable perturbation that isolates the fusion effect. If weighted fusion improves accuracy, it opens a family of weighted-fusion multiprofile configurations to exploit in remaining budget; if not, concat is confirmed as the better fusion and we can pivot to testing alternative RNA encoders (scvi_n200, pca_n2000) in the transformer+concat setting. This is the best use of experiment 3 because it is the cheapest informative step: same architecture as config_005 so expected training cost is comparable (~3.5–4.0 GPU hours, slightly less since weighted fusion avoids the dimensionality increase of concat), keeping total spend around ~8.8 GPU hours with 6 experiments still available.

The current best (config_010, 0.520 acc) uses scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The most important untested design axis is the RNA encoder: scgpt is a large pretrained transformer, while scvi_n200 is a compact VAE that may capture different latent structure. config_045 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) isolates the RNA encoder change while holding all other hyperparameters at their best-known values. If scvi_n200 matches scgpt, we gain a cheaper encoder for future runs; if it underperforms, we confirm scgpt's value and can focus remaining budget on image-encoder or aggregation variations. Expected cost is moderate (~2.0–2.5 GPU hrs), slightly below config_010's 2.86 hrs since scvi_n200 is a smaller model than scgpt, while the expensive imagenet_vit_l and transformer aggregation remain. With 6 experiments left, this is the highest-information experiment: it either validates the current RNA choice or opens a cheaper alternative before we fine-tune around the optimum.

The dominant finding from the history is that switching the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 yielded a massive accuracy jump (0.520 → 0.725) while keeping all other settings identical (multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted). config_045 is now the clear best. The next most informative single-variable change is the image encoder: we have only tested imagenet_vit_l with scvi_n200. config_035 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) directly tests whether the image modality's contribution is encoder-dependent. If resnet50 is competitive, it confirms the RNA encoder is the key driver and opens cheaper future configurations; if imagenet_vit_l is clearly superior, it validates the current best and focuses remaining budget on other axes (e.g., fusion or aggregation). This is a high-information experiment because the image-encoder dimension is completely unexplored with the best-performing RNA encoder. Expected cost: resnet50 is smaller than ViT-L, so this should be somewhat cheaper than config_045's 3.60 GPU-hr, likely ~2.5–3.0 GPU-hr, making it a cost-efficient probe.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + weighted fusion (config_045, 0.725 acc) is the best configuration, and transformer aggregation is the only aggregation tested with this top combination. The key uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation layer is actually contributing meaningful performance over a simpler avgpool, or whether the strong scvi_n200 encoder makes the aggregation strategy less critical. Config_003 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) isolates this question by changing only the aggregation from transformer to avgpool while keeping all other top-performing components fixed. If avgpool performs comparably (~0.70+), it confirms a cheaper architecture is viable, saving GPU hours for the remaining 4 experiments to explore other directions. If it drops significantly, we confirm transformer is essential and can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning other aspects. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-low (~2-2.5 GPU hours), roughly 30-40% cheaper than the transformer-based config_045 (3.60 GPU hours), since avgpool eliminates the transformer self-attention layers over profiles.

Evidence: config_045 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is the current best at 0.725 accuracy / 0.685 F1. All scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer experiments confirm this architecture family is optimal. The only untested single-variable change from the best config is fusion type (concat vs weighted). While weighted outperformed concat in the scgpt experiments (0.520 vs 0.507), scvi_n200 produces fundamentally different (richer, denoised) representations where the relative benefit of weighted vs concat fusion is uncertain. This experiment tests whether concat fusion could match or exceed weighted fusion when paired with scvi_n200's representations. It is the best use of experiment 7 because: (1) it is a minimal, interpretable perturbation of the current best, (2) it is cheap (~3.5 GPU hours, similar to config_045's 3.60), keeping total cost manageable, and (3) with 3 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out a small fusion improvement lets us lock in the best configuration confidently. Expected relative cost: low, comparable to config_045.

The evidence strongly identifies config_045 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.725 acc) as the best configuration, with every tested variation (avgpool, concat, resnet50, singleprofile) reducing accuracy. The remaining question is whether a cheaper combination of components (resnet50 + avgpool instead of imagenet_vit_l + transformer) can achieve comparable accuracy at lower cost, or whether the transformer aggregation and ViT-L image encoder are both essential for peak performance. Config_050 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted) directly tests this: it keeps the proven scvi_n200 encoder and weighted fusion while swapping both the image encoder and aggregation to cheaper alternatives. If it lands near 0.71–0.72, it confirms config_045 is the accuracy winner; if it drops to ~0.69–0.70, it validates that the transformer+ViT-L combination is critical. This is the best use of experiment 8 because (1) no untested configuration is likely to beat 0.725, so the goal shifts to confirming the landscape and identifying cost-efficient alternatives, (2) it reduces uncertainty about which components drive the performance gap, and (3) with 2 experiments remaining, it preserves budget for a final confirmation run. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-low (~2.5–3.5 GPU hours), cheaper than config_045 (3.60) and much cheaper than config_035 (6.22) due to avgpool replacing transformer and resnet50 replacing ViT-L.

Evidence: The top-performing region is clearly scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, with config_045 (vit_l + weighted) at 0.7250 as the current best, config_007 (vit_l + concat) at 0.7207, and config_035 (resnet50 + weighted) at 0.7131. The remaining untested configuration in this high-performing region is config_032 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat). This experiment tests whether the resnet50 + concat combination with transformer aggregation is competitive, completing the 2×2 factorial (image encoder × fusion) within the best aggregation setting. While I expect it to land around 0.71 (below config_045), it is the most informative remaining test in the proven high-accuracy region and rules out any unexpected synergy between resnet50 and concat fusion. No other untested configuration (avgpool variants, singleprofile, or non-scvi encoders) has a realistic chance of exceeding 0.7250. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-high (~5–6 GPU hours, comparable to config_035's 6.22), since it uses resnet50 with transformer aggregation. This is a justified expense given it is the last untested point in the top-performing subspace and only one experiment remains after this one.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile (config_045, 0.725 acc) as the best configuration found. The only major untested variable across the top-performing family is the RNA encoder: pca_n2000 has never been tested. config_006 pairs pca_n2000 with all other settings at their empirically best values (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile), directly testing whether a simpler linear encoder could match or exceed scvi_n200. While I expect scvi_n200 to remain superior (scgpt, a more complex learned model, already underperformed it), this is the highest-value remaining exploration because it is the only untested axis that could plausibly shift accuracy in either direction. As the final experiment, it either reveals a surprise gain or definitively confirms config_045 as the optimum. Expected cost: ~3.0–3.5 GPU hours (PCA encoding is cheaper than scVI, while the ViT-L image encoder and transformer aggregation dominate runtime), making it a modest addition to the 38.09 GPU hours already spent.

With no prior experiments, the primary uncertainty is whether a multimodal multiprofile pipeline outperforms simpler baselines and which component choices matter most. Config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is a well-balanced 'middle' configuration: it uses a proven RNA encoder (scvi_n200), a standard and efficient image encoder (resnet50), a lightweight aggregation (avgpool), and a simple weighted fusion. This tests the core hypothesis that combining RNA and image modalities with multiprofile aggregation is beneficial, while keeping training cost moderate (resnet50 + avgpool are both cheaper than ViT-L + transformer). If it performs strongly, subsequent experiments can isolate whether upgrading to transformer aggregation or ViT-L yields meaningful gains; if it underperforms, I can pivot to single-modality baselines. Expected relative cost: moderate (~40-50% of the most expensive configs like ViT-L + transformer), making it an efficient first probe that establishes a competitive baseline without consuming disproportionate GPU budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200/resnet50, avgpool, weighted → 0.678 acc, 5.90 GPU-h), evidence is very sparse. The most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality is actually contributing signal or adding noise. Config_002 is the direct RNA-only ablation of config_001 (same scvi_n200 encoder, same multiprofile/avgpool setup, no image branch), so any accuracy difference isolates the value of the image modality and the fusion step. If RNA-only matches or exceeds 0.678, the fusion is not helping and we should pivot to improving the RNA pipeline or trying different encoders; if it falls well below, multimodal is confirmed as the right direction and we can invest remaining budget in stronger image encoders (ViT-L) or better aggregation (transformer). This experiment is also the cheapest multimodal-related test (~3–4 GPU-h, no image encoder), preserving budget for later exploitation. It is the single highest-information, lowest-cost next step under the 8-experiment remainder.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.6776 acc, outperforming RNA-only config_002 (0.6501) by ~2.7%, confirming the image modality contributes meaningfully. However, we have no data on how a stronger image encoder (ViT-L vs ResNet50) affects performance. This experiment (config_008) is a clean single-variable change from config_001—only the image encoder upgrades from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l—while keeping scvi_n200, avgpool, weighted fusion, and multiprofile fixed. It directly tests whether a more expressive image representation (ViT-L, ~307M params vs ResNet50's ~25M) can amplify the multimodal advantage. This is the best next step because: (1) the image encoder is the largest untested design lever with the highest expected impact on accuracy; (2) it isolates one variable for clear attribution; (3) with 7 experiments remaining, establishing whether ViT-L helps now guides whether to invest in transformer aggregation or VIT-L-based configs later. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-high, roughly 8–10 GPU hours (ViT-L forward/backward is ~3–5× costlier than ResNet50, while the RNA pipeline is unchanged), so it is more expensive than config_001 but justified by the potential accuracy gain.

Evidence: config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the clear best at 0.7062 acc, outperforming the resnet50 variant (config_001, 0.6776) by ~3% and the RNA-only baseline (config_002, 0.6501) by ~5.6%. This establishes that the VIT-L image encoder + weighted fusion + multiprofile setup is the strongest direction. Uncertainty: whether the simple avgpool aggregation is the bottleneck for combining multiple profiles, or whether a learned transformer aggregation could capture richer inter-profile interactions. This experiment tests that single change: replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping the proven weighted fusion and VIT-L encoder. It is the best next step because it directly extends the best configuration along the most impactful untested axis (aggregation mechanism), and a transformer over profiles could yield a meaningful accuracy gain. Expected cost: moderate-to-high (~6-7 GPU hours) due to the transformer aggregation layer on top of the VIT-L multimodal pipeline, somewhat above config_008's 4.82 hrs, but justified by the high expected accuracy ceiling.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_041 (acc=0.7250, F1=0.6847) using multimodal + multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The progression clearly shows that imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 and transformer > avgpool, both with scvi_n200 RNA encoder. The remaining untested variable within this winning recipe is the fusion strategy (weighted vs. concat). Question: Does concat fusion outperform weighted fusion when combined with transformer aggregation and the ViT-L image encoder? This is a single-variable change from the current best, making it a clean exploitation step. Why this is the best use: With 5 experiments remaining, confirming or improving the fusion strategy on the strongest known architecture is the highest-value next step. If concat improves accuracy, it establishes a new best; if not, it confirms weighted fusion and frees the remaining budget to explore RNA encoder alternatives (e.g., scgpt). Expected cost: ~3.6 GPU hours (same architecture as config_041), keeping total well within budget.

The current best (config_041, 0.7250 acc) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The image encoder and aggregation choices are now well-characterized (vit_l >> resnet50; transformer > avgpool), but the RNA encoder has only been tested as scvi_n200 in the top-performing setup. Config_015 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) isolates the RNA encoder variable by swapping scvi_n200 for scgpt while holding all other factors constant. scgpt is a fundamentally different learned representation (generative vs. variational), so it may capture complementary biological signal that could push accuracy above 0.725. This is the highest-value exploration step: it either confirms scvi_n200 is optimal (freeing us to exploit the current best) or reveals a new direction with 4 experiments remaining. Expected cost: ~4.0–4.5 GPU hours, comparable to config_041 (3.60 h) since the dominant costs (ViT-L image encoder, transformer aggregation) are unchanged; scgpt is slightly heavier than scvi_n200 but the difference is modest relative to the image-side compute.

Evidence: The best config so far is config_041 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.7250 acc. We've confirmed that scgpt is a poor RNA encoder (0.5200 in config_015) and that imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted is the strongest image/aggregation/fusion stack. However, pca_n2000 — the third and only remaining RNA encoder — has never been tested in any multimodal setting. This experiment tests whether pca_n2000 (a linear dimensionality-reduction encoder) can match or approach scvi_n200 in the best-known architecture, or whether scvi_n200's learned latent space is essential. Clarifying this is important because if pca_n2000 is competitive, it offers a cheaper RNA pathway and opens the remaining 3 experiments to fine-tuning around it; if it underperforms significantly, we can confidently lock in scvi_n200 and spend remaining budget on marginal refinements (e.g., singleprofile variant config_049). Expected relative cost: moderate — PCA encoding is cheaper than scvi_n200, but imagenet_vit_l and transformer aggregation keep total cost comparable to config_041 (~3–4 GPU hours), so this is not a high-cost gamble for an untested dimension.

Evidence: Our current best (config_041, 0.7250 acc) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation + weighted fusion in multiprofile mode. All multiprofile variants with these encoders have been tested, and the improvements from each component are well-characterized. However, singleprofile multimodal with the best encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) is completely untested. This experiment tests whether removing the multiprofile aggregation step (aggregation=None) and fusing the two modalities directly via weighted combination can match or exceed 0.7250. It is the highest-value untested direction: if it succeeds, it may offer a comparable-accuracy, lower-cost alternative (no aggregation step, expected ~3–3.5 GPU hours, slightly cheaper than config_041's 3.60); if it fails, it confirms config_041 as the optimal architecture among available options, allowing the final experiment to focus on a last refinement. With only 2 experiments remaining, resolving this single unexplored architectural axis is the best use of the next slot.

Evidence: The top-3 configurations (config_041: 0.725, config_039: 0.721, config_008: 0.706) all use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + multimodal, with transformer aggregation and weighted/concat fusion. Transformer > avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706) and weighted ≈ concat (0.725 vs 0.721) are well-supported. config_044 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) is the only remaining untested configuration within this proven high-performing encoder/profile region. Question: Does the transformer aggregation advantage persist under concat fusion, or could avgpool+concat be a competitive (and potentially cheaper) alternative? This is the best use of experiment 9 because (a) it is the closest untested variant to the current best, giving the highest probability of a competitive result, (b) it reduces residual uncertainty about whether the 0.725 ceiling is truly set or whether a different aggregation-fusion pairing could close the gap, and (c) it informs the final experiment: if it lands near 0.72, the last slot can be spent on a targeted refinement; if it drops significantly, it confirms config_041 as the robust optimum. Expected cost: moderate, roughly 4–5 GPU hours (avgpool is cheaper than transformer, but ViT-L image encoding and multiprofile aggregation keep it comparable to config_008's 4.82 hrs).

Evidence: The best result so far is config_041 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725). All four aggregation/fusion combinations with scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l+multiprofile have been tested, exhausting that design space. The only untested configuration retaining three of the four best components (scvi_n200, transformer, weighted) is config_022, which swaps imagenet_vit_l for resnet50. Question: Does the transformer aggregation's benefit (which gave ~2% over avgpool with vit_l) transfer to resnet50, potentially narrowing the encoder gap? This is the closest untested configuration to the current best and the only one with a non-trivial chance of approaching or exceeding 0.725. As the final experiment, it provides the highest expected marginal information about the architecture interaction while confirming that the vit_l+transformer+weighted combination is indeed optimal. Expected cost: ~2.5–3.5 GPU hours (resnet50 is smaller than ViT-L, so cheaper than config_041's 3.60), keeping total budget modest.

With no prior experiments, the key uncertainty is whether a multimodal setup provides a meaningful accuracy baseline and at what cost. Config_009 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, weighted fusion) is the simplest multimodal configuration in the space: it uses the cheapest RNA encoder (PCA, no learned encoder), a standard mid-size image encoder (ResNet50 rather than the more expensive ViT-L), single-profile (no multiprofile aggregation overhead), and a straightforward weighted fusion. This establishes a clear multimodal accuracy baseline at moderate expected cost (roughly 1x relative to the cheapest single-modality runs, and well below multiprofile+ViL configurations). It is the best first experiment because it directly tests the core hypothesis of the study (does combining RNA and image features help?) at the lowest multimodal cost, giving a reference point against which I can later evaluate whether multiprofile aggregation, richer encoders (scgpt/scvi), transformer aggregation, or ViT-L images are worth their additional GPU hours.

With only one completed experiment (config_009: multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, weighted fusion → 52.3% acc, 0.87 GPU-h), the most informative next step is to test whether multiprofile aggregation provides a meaningful gain over the single-profile baseline. config_003 is the minimal, controlled extension of config_009: it keeps the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (resnet50), and fusion strategy (weighted), changing only the profile setting from single to multi with avgpool aggregation. This isolates the effect of multiprofile aggregation, which is the single most impactful architectural axis in the remaining search space (the majority of untested configs are multiprofile). A positive result would justify investing subsequent experiments in optimizing within the multiprofile space (encoder upgrades, transformer aggregation, concat fusion); a null or negative result would redirect effort toward single-profile encoder improvements or modality ablations. Expected relative cost: moderately higher than config_009 (~1.0–1.3 GPU-h) due to processing multiple profiles and the avgpool aggregation step, but still well within the cheaper tier compared to ViT-L or transformer-aggregation configurations. This is the best use of experiment 2 because it reduces the largest source of uncertainty (single vs. multi profile) at low cost and directly shapes the exploitation strategy for the remaining 7 experiments.

Evidence: config_003 (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.639 accuracy vs config_009 (singleprofile, no aggregation, weighted) at 0.523, a large ~11.6 pp jump driven by multiprofile aggregation. The key open question is whether avgpool is the best aggregation strategy or whether a transformer-based aggregation can capture richer cross-profile interactions. config_024 is identical to config_003 (pca_n2000, resnet50, multiprofile, weighted fusion) except it replaces avgpool with transformer aggregation, making it a clean single-variable A/B test against the current best. This is the most architecturally significant design choice remaining: if transformer aggregation substantially improves over avgpool, it opens a high-accuracy direction for the remaining 6 experiments; if it is comparable, we can confidently lock in avgpool and pivot to encoder or fusion variations. Expected relative cost: transformer attention over the profile dimension adds moderate compute over the avgpool baseline, so I estimate ~12–14 GPU hours, roughly 15–30% more expensive than config_003's 10.6 hours. This is a worthwhile investment given the potential accuracy gain and the 7 experiments still available.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_003 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.639 acc. Multiprofile with avgpool clearly outperforms singleprofile (0.523) and transformer aggregation (0.573). The only untested variation on this exact architecture is the fusion strategy: config_008 swaps weighted fusion for concat fusion while keeping all other settings identical (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, multiprofile). This isolates a single variable and directly tests whether concatenating the two modality representations (preserving full information) beats their weighted sum. It is the cheapest logical extension of the current best, with expected cost comparable to config_003 (~10–11 GPU hours, similar multiprofile avgpool pipeline). Under the limited budget (6 experiments remaining), this targeted exploitation of the strongest configuration maximizes the chance of finding an incremental improvement without spending GPU hours on a large architectural jump.

Evidence: config_003 (multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the best at 0.639 acc, and the key architectural choices (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) are well-supported. The main untested lever for improvement is the image encoder: ViT-L pretrained on ImageNet should provide substantially richer visual representations than ResNet50. This experiment (config_051: pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) isolates the image encoder upgrade while keeping all other proven settings fixed, directly testing whether a stronger visual backbone can push accuracy beyond 0.639. It is the best use of experiment 5 because it exploits the strongest known architecture while probing the single most impactful untested component (image encoder quality). Expected relative cost: moderate-to-high, likely ~15-25 GPU hours (ViT-L is larger than ResNet50, but avgpool+weighted keeps aggregation/fusion overhead low, similar in structure to config_003's 10.60 hrs). This is well within remaining budget and justified by the expected accuracy gain.

The current best is config_003 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.639 acc / 10.60 GPU-hr. Key evidence: multiprofile >> singleprofile, avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat fusion, and imagenet_vit_l ≈ resnet50 (0.635 vs 0.639) at lower cost (7.02 vs 10.60). The largest remaining uncertainty is whether the RNA encoder matters—pca_n2000 is a simple linear projection, while scgpt is a deep pretrained generative model that may capture richer biological structure. config_006 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) directly tests this by swapping only the RNA encoder in the best-performing architecture, while using the cheaper image encoder. If scgpt improves accuracy, it opens a new optimization axis for the remaining 4 experiments; if not, it confirms PCA sufficiency and we can focus on other factors. Expected cost: moderate (~8–12 GPU-hr), slightly above config_051 due to scgpt forward passes but below config_003 since vit_l is lighter than resnet50.

The evidence strongly supports multiprofile + avgpool + weighted as the optimal architecture (config_003: 0.639 acc, config_051: 0.635 acc), with pca_n2000 as the best RNA encoder tested and resnet50/vit_l performing nearly identically for images. The key untested dimension is the RNA encoder: scgpt underperformed badly (0.542), but scvi_n200 (a 200-dim learned variational representation) is a fundamentally different model and remains untested. config_022 pairs scvi_n200 with the proven-best settings (multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool, weighted), directly testing whether a learned low-dim RNA representation can match or exceed the 2000-dim PCA baseline. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve with 3 experiments remaining: if scvi_n200 matches pca_n2000, it opens cheaper multimodal combinations; if it underperforms like scgpt, we can confidently lock in pca_n2000 and focus remaining budget on fine-tuning image/fusion choices. Expected cost: moderate, roughly 8–11 GPU hours (scvi_n200's 200-dim representation is smaller than pca_n2000's 2000-dim, so likely at or below config_003's 10.60 GPU hours), making it an efficient experiment relative to the information gained.

The current best is config_022 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.678). The image encoder comparison (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) was previously tested only with pca_n2000 (config_003: 0.639 vs config_051: 0.635), yielding a near-tie. However, with the stronger learned scvi_n200 RNA representation, the interaction with the image encoder may differ—ViT-L's richer spatial features could complement scvi's latent embeddings more effectively than ResNet50's. config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) is the cleanest single-variable extension of the current best, isolating the image encoder upgrade while keeping the proven optimal aggregation (avgpool) and fusion (weighted). This is the highest-value test: if it improves, it gives a stronger baseline for the final 2 experiments; if not, it confirms ResNet50 suffices and redirects remaining budget to other axes. Expected cost is ~7-8 GPU hours (comparable to config_051 at 7.02), which is moderate and leaves ample budget for the remaining two experiments.

The best result so far is config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) at 0.706 accuracy. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l as the best image encoder. However, avgpool outperformed transformer only when paired with the linear pca_n2000 encoder (0.639 vs 0.573). With scvi_n200 producing richer, nonlinear latent representations and vit_l producing more structured visual features, a transformer aggregation could capture inter-profile attention patterns that simple averaging misses. This experiment tests whether the transformer aggregation, which underperformed with a linear encoder, can succeed with the learned nonlinear encoders. It is a logical exploitation of the best-known component choices while exploring the one remaining aggregation mechanism. Expected cost is moderate (~5-8 GPU hours), comparable to config_048's 4.82 hours, since transformer with these encoders should not be dramatically more expensive than avgpool (cf. config_024 at 6.61h vs config_003 at 10.60h). This is the best use of experiment 9: it has a realistic chance of exceeding 0.706 if nonlinear representations benefit from attention-based profile interaction, while keeping total budget well-controlled for the final experiment.

Evidence: config_016 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is the clear best at 0.7250 acc, with scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and multiprofile all consistently outperforming alternatives. The only untested variant with this exact encoder+aggregation combination is concat fusion (config_020). While weighted has beaten concat in prior tests (0.639 vs 0.619 with avgpool), the interaction between transformer aggregation and concat fusion is untested, and the margin was modest. This is the last experiment, so the goal is to either find a configuration that surpasses 0.7250 or confirm the current best. config_020 is the single most logical extension of the top performer, isolating the one remaining untested variable. Expected cost: comparable to config_016 (~3.5–5 GPU hours) since it shares the same encoders and transformer aggregation; concat fusion may marginally widen the final layer but overall training cost should be similar to config_016's 3.60 GPU hours.

With no prior experiments, the key uncertainty is whether the strongest multimodal combination (scgpt RNA encoder + ViT-L image encoder) with multiprofile aggregation yields a high-performing baseline. config_001 tests this 'strong multimodal' hypothesis using avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion—a simpler, more robust fusion strategy than transformer-based approaches. This is the best first experiment because: (1) it is likely to be near the top of the accuracy range, establishing a high reference point for the remaining 9 experiments; (2) if it performs well, subsequent experiments can efficiently explore variations (fusion type, aggregation, image encoder); if it underperforms, it signals that the architecture needs rethinking; (3) it avoids the extra cost of transformer aggregation while still testing the core multimodal hypothesis. Expected relative cost: high (ViT-L + scgpt + multiprofile processing), but moderate compared to transformer-aggregation configs like config_014 or config_032.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted → acc 0.542), the evidence is extremely sparse and the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal combination is actually contributing over a strong unimodal baseline. config_036 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) is the cleanest ablation of config_001: it keeps the same RNA encoder (scgpt), same profile setting (multiprofile), and same aggregation (avgpool), removing only the image branch and fusion. If RNA-only achieves accuracy close to 0.542, the image modality is not adding value and I should pivot to cheaper RNA-focused or image-focused configs for the remaining 8 experiments. If it drops substantially, multimodal is confirmed as the right direction and I can then explore fusion/aggregation/encoder variants within the multimodal family. Expected cost: roughly 1.5–2.0 GPU hours (no ViT-L image forward/backward), making it cheaper than config_001 while answering the highest-leverage design question early in the budget.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.542 acc but only marginally beats RNA-only config_036 (0.530 acc, 0.515 F1), and actually loses on F1 (0.483 vs 0.515). This suggests the current weighted fusion strategy may not be effectively combining the two modalities. Question: config_006 isolates the fusion mechanism by switching from weighted to concat while keeping everything else identical (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, multiprofile). This is the cleanest single-variable ablation from our best result. Why this experiment: With 7 experiments remaining, I need to determine whether multimodal fusion can meaningfully outperform RNA-only before investing in more complex variants (transformer aggregation, different encoders). If concat fusion improves accuracy/F1, it validates the multimodal direction and guides subsequent experiments toward better fusion+aggregation combos. If it doesn't, the bottleneck is elsewhere (aggregation or image encoder), and I can pivot. Expected cost: similar to config_001 (~2.9 GPU hours), since the architecture is identical except for the fusion layer.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the best at 0.542 acc, and weighted fusion clearly beats concat (0.542 vs 0.518). The only untested dimension on this top configuration is the aggregation method—avgpool has been used in all three completed experiments, so we have no evidence about whether transformer aggregation could better capture inter-profile relationships. Question: Does replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (while keeping the proven scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion stack) improve validation accuracy? This is the highest-uncertainty, highest-potential-reward single-variable change from the current best. Rationale: With 6 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest configuration while probing the one untested architectural axis (aggregation) is the most efficient use of the next slot. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-high (~4–5 GPU hrs), since transformer attention over multiple profiles adds compute over avgpool but is still lighter than the concat-fusion variant (7.18 hrs); this is justified because the expected accuracy gain from better profile interaction modeling is substantial.

Evidence: The best config so far (config_001: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.542 accuracy, but the RNA-only baseline (config_036: scgpt + avgpool) reaches 0.530, meaning the image modality contributes only ~1.2%. All multimodal tests have used imagenet_vit_l, leaving the image encoder choice unexplored. Weighted fusion clearly outperforms concat (0.542 vs 0.518), and avgpool beats transformer aggregation (0.542 vs 0.520) with this RNA encoder. Question: Will switching the image encoder to ResNet50 (which captures different morphological/spatial features than a ViT) improve the multimodal contribution beyond the current 1.2% gain, while keeping all other settings at their best-performing values? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a clean single-variable change from the current best, directly testing whether the modest image benefit is encoder-specific. ResNet50 is substantially smaller than ViT-L (~23M vs ~300M params), so the expected training cost is lower—roughly 1.5–2.5 GPU hours vs. the 2.94 for config_001—making it a cost-efficient exploration. If it matches or beats 0.542, we gain a cheaper best config; if it underperforms, we confirm ViT-L is the right image encoder and can focus remaining budget on other dimensions (RNA encoder, profile setting).

Evidence: config_001 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, multiprofile) is the best at 0.5420 acc, and all completed experiments used scgpt as the RNA encoder. The only other RNA encoder tested (in rna_only config_036) was also scgpt, so we have zero evidence on whether scvi_n200 or pca_n2000 could match or exceed scgpt in the multimodal setting. Question: Does swapping scgpt for scvi_n200 in the best-performing multimodal configuration (imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) maintain or improve accuracy? This directly tests the RNA encoder axis, which is the most important unexplored dimension given that all top results used scgpt. If scvi_n200 performs comparably, it likely trains cheaper (VAE vs. transformer-based encoder), improving the accuracy-per-GPU-hour ratio. If it underperforms, we confirm scgpt is the right choice and can focus remaining budget on other axes (e.g., single profile, resnet50 variants). Expected cost: moderate, roughly 2.0–2.5 GPU hours (scvi_n200 is lighter than scgpt, but imagenet_vit_l and multiprofile aggregation keep it in the same ballpark as config_001's 2.94 hrs). This is the best use of experiment 6 because it exploits the strongest configuration while reducing uncertainty on a high-impact design choice, leaving 4 experiments to exploit whichever RNA encoder wins.

The dominant finding is that switching the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 (config_026) produced a large jump to 0.706 accuracy, far exceeding all scgpt-based configs (~0.52–0.54). With only 3 experiments remaining after this one, the priority is to exploit the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted-fusion + multiprofile combination and test whether the aggregation method can be improved. config_027 is a single-variable extension of the best config, replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation. While transformer was slightly worse than avgpool in the scgpt experiments (0.520 vs 0.542), scvi_n200's learned latent representation may interact differently with attention-based aggregation, potentially capturing richer inter-profile relationships. This is the highest-information next step: if it improves, we have a stronger champion; if it does not, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can focus remaining budget on other axes (e.g., image encoder or singleprofile). Expected cost is moderate, roughly 5–6 GPU hours (comparable to config_026's 4.82 h with a small overhead for the transformer aggregation layer), keeping total spend well within budget.

Evidence: The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile dramatically outperforms all scgpt-based configs (0.725 vs ~0.54). Within this family, transformer aggregation (config_027, 0.7250) beats avgpool (config_026, 0.7062) by ~2%, and weighted fusion has consistently outperformed concat in all prior comparisons (e.g., config_001 vs config_006). Question: config_048 tests the one remaining untested combination within our proven best architecture—scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat—directly probing whether concat fusion might complement transformer aggregation differently than it does with avgpool. Why this is the best use of experiment 8: It is the lowest-risk, highest-information exploitation of our strongest result, testing the last untested variable in the top-performing family. Expected cost is moderate (~3.5–4 GPU hrs), comparable to config_027 (3.60 hrs) since the architecture is identical except for the fusion operation. Even if it does not surpass config_027, it definitively closes the fusion question for this architecture, allowing the final experiment to be directed at a more exploratory direction (e.g., singleprofile or an alternative image encoder) with full confidence about the current best.

Evidence: config_027 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) is the clear best at 0.725 accuracy, and the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l encoder pair is strongly validated. The only major untested dimension with these top encoders is the profile setting (singleprofile vs multiprofile). Question: config_022 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted, singleprofile) tests whether removing the aggregation step and processing a single profile directly can match or exceed the multiprofile+transformer pipeline. This is valuable because singleprofile eliminates the aggregation bottleneck entirely, and with the strong scvi_n200 encoder the per-profile signal may already be sufficient. Why this is the best use: with only 1 experiment remaining after this one, I need to either find a configuration that beats 0.725 or confirm the ceiling. Singleprofile is the only structurally different unexplored axis with the proven best encoders. It is also expected to be cheaper (~2.5–3.0 GPU hours vs 3.60 for config_027) since it skips the transformer aggregation step, improving the cost-accuracy tradeoff if it performs comparably. If it underperforms, it confirms multiprofile+transformer is essential and locks in config_027 as the final answer.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted as the optimal architecture (config_027: 0.725 acc), with imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder. The only remaining untested variable within this top-performing family is the image encoder: config_033 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted) tests whether the smaller resnet50 backbone can match or approach vit_l's performance when paired with the superior scvi_n200 RNA encoder. From the scgpt comparisons (config_001 vs config_009), vit_l outperformed resnet50 by ~1.7%, but scvi_n200's stronger representations may interact differently with the image modality. This is the best use of the final experiment because: (1) it tests the one remaining design choice in the proven-best architecture, (2) if resnet50 matches vit_l, it offers a cheaper alternative for deployment, and (3) if it underperforms, it definitively confirms config_027 as the optimal configuration. Expected cost is moderate (~2.5–3.5 GPU hours), slightly cheaper than config_027 since resnet50 has fewer parameters than ViT-L, keeping total budget reasonable.

With no prior evidence, the most important uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion (image + RNA) provides meaningful accuracy gains over single-modality baselines, and which component combination yields a strong starting reference. Config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) tests this core hypothesis with a well-balanced, moderate-complexity setup: scgpt is a strong pretrained single-cell RNA encoder (more biologically informed than PCA, potentially more expressive than scvi_n200), resnet50 is a solid image backbone that is substantially cheaper than imagenet_vit_l, avgpool is a low-cost aggregation, and weighted fusion is a standard, interpretable fusion strategy. This experiment establishes a strong multimodal baseline at moderate compute cost (estimated ~40-50% of a ViT-L + transformer configuration), leaving ample GPU budget to later explore upgrades (ViT-L, transformer aggregation, scgpt+ViT-L) or single-modality baselines. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can exploit by upgrading individual components; if it underperforms, we gain early signal that multimodal fusion or the chosen encoders need rethinking, saving budget from chasing a weak direction.

With only one completed experiment (config_008: scgpt+resnet50+avgpool+weighted → 52.5% acc, 4.42 GPU hrs), the evidence is sparse and the biggest uncertainty is whether the image encoder is a bottleneck. Config_007 changes exactly one variable from the baseline—upgrading the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L—while keeping scgpt, avgpool, and weighted fusion identical. This gives a clean A/B comparison to isolate the image-encoder contribution. ViT-L is substantially more expressive than ResNet50, so the potential accuracy upside is large; if it helps, the image branch is a key lever and we can exploit it further; if it doesn't, we rule out the image encoder and redirect effort toward RNA encoding, aggregation, or fusion. Expected cost is moderate-to-high (~7–9 GPU hrs) due to the larger ViT-L backbone, but with 8 experiments remaining the budget can absorb one expensive high-information experiment. This is the best use of experiment 2 because it targets the single highest-impact design axis with minimal confounding.

Evidence: config_007 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) achieved the best accuracy (0.542) at a lower cost (2.94 GPU hrs) than config_008 (scgpt + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, 0.525 acc, 4.42 GPU hrs), suggesting the ViT-L image encoder is the stronger backbone. Uncertainty: we have only tested one fusion strategy (weighted) and one aggregation (avgpool), so it is unclear whether concat fusion could further improve on the best result. Question tested: config_016 changes only the fusion from weighted to concat while keeping the best-performing backbone (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool), directly isolating the fusion effect. Why this is the best next experiment: it is a minimal, cheap (~3 GPU hrs, comparable to config_007) exploitation of the current best direction, reducing uncertainty about fusion before committing to larger architectural changes (transformer aggregation, different RNA encoders, or singleprofile). With 7 experiments remaining, establishing the optimal fusion for the best backbone early allows subsequent experiments to build on a stronger foundation.

Evidence: All three completed experiments use scgpt as the RNA encoder, so we have no information about whether scvi_n200 or pca_n2000 could outperform it. The best result so far is config_007 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.542), and weighted fusion with imagenet_vit_l appears to be the strongest image-side combination. Question: Does replacing scgpt with scvi_n200 (a learned generative RNA encoder) while keeping the best image encoder and fusion improve accuracy? This is the most important unexplored axis—RNA encoder choice—since it could reveal a fundamentally better representation. Why this experiment: It directly extends the best-performing configuration by swapping only the RNA encoder, isolating that variable. It also has moderate expected cost (~3–4 GPU hours, comparable to config_007's 2.94 h since both use a learned RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l and avgpool), making it an efficient use of the remaining 6 experiments to reduce uncertainty about the RNA encoder before committing to further aggregation or profile-setting variations.

Evidence: config_019 (scvi_n200, vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.706 accuracy, dramatically outperforming all scgpt-based configs (~0.52-0.54), establishing scvi_n200 as the dominant RNA encoder. Within scgpt configs, weighted fusion > concat (0.542 vs 0.518) and vit_l > resnet50 (0.542 vs 0.525). The only untested dimension with the best-known components is aggregation: all top configs used avgpool. Question: Does transformer aggregation improve upon avgpool when paired with the strong scvi_n200 + vit_l + weighted combination? This is the most informative exploitation step because it tests whether the remaining architectural lever (aggregation) can push accuracy beyond 0.706. If transformer helps, it opens a new high-performing family; if not, we confirm avgpool is sufficient and can focus remaining budget on singleprofile or other refinements. Expected cost: transformer aggregation adds self-attention over profiles, so I estimate ~5-7 GPU hours (moderately above config_019's 4.82), keeping total budget well within reasonable bounds with 5 experiments remaining.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the best component pair (0.706–0.725 accuracy vs ~0.52–0.54 for scgpt), and transformer aggregation with weighted fusion is the current best (config_049, 0.725). The most important unexplored design axis is multiprofile vs singleprofile: we have only tested singleprofile with weaker encoders. Config_020 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) tests whether removing the multiprofile aggregation step helps or hurts when the RNA encoder is already strong. If singleprofile matches or beats 0.725, it would be a simpler, cheaper architecture; if it underperforms, it confirms that multiprofile + transformer aggregation captures essential profile-level information. This resolves a key architectural uncertainty with the strongest known components. Expected cost: lower than config_049 (~3.6 GPU hrs) since singleprofile eliminates the aggregation step, likely ~2–3 GPU hours, making it a cost-efficient experiment.

The current best (config_049: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.725 acc) sits in the clearly dominant family (scvi_n200 >> scgpt, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, multiprofile >> singleprofile). The only untested combination within this top family is transformer aggregation with concat fusion (config_011). While weighted fusion has outperformed concat in other settings (config_007 vs 016: 0.542 vs 0.518), transformer aggregation already performs an attention-weighted combination of profile tokens, so concat may provide complementary raw information that a subsequent linear layer can exploit differently. Testing config_011 completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the best encoder pair, directly clarifying whether 0.725 is the ceiling for this family or whether a small fusion-method gain is available. With 3 experiments left, locking in the optimal fusion for the top family is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve. Expected cost: moderate (~4–5 GPU hours), comparable to config_049 (3.60) but slightly higher due to the larger concatenated feature vector, consistent with the concat premium seen in config_016 (7.18) vs config_007 (2.94).

The current best is config_049 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725), with config_011 (same but concat fusion, acc=0.721) a close second. All top performers share the transformer+weighted architecture with scvi_n200 and ViT-L. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation benefit is driven by the learned SCVI representation or is more general. config_043 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) directly tests this: if PCA achieves comparable accuracy (~0.70+), the architecture (transformer + weighted fusion) is the primary driver and config_049 is confirmed as the ceiling; if it drops substantially, it validates that SCVI's learned latent space is essential and no simpler encoder will close the gap. This is the best use of experiment 8 because it reduces uncertainty about the most important design axis (RNA encoder quality vs. architecture) with moderate cost (PCA encoding is far cheaper than SCVI; expected ~3–3.5 GPU hours, comparable to config_049's 3.60). With 2 experiments remaining, this information will guide whether the final experiment should attempt a marginal architectural tweak or simply confirm the best configuration.

Evidence: The top-3 configs (config_049: 0.725, config_011: 0.721, config_019: 0.706) all use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile, with transformer aggregation clearly outperforming avgpool (~0.02 gap) and weighted/concat fusion nearly tied. Question: config_015 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) is the only remaining untested cell in the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the proven best encoder pair, completing the search space. It tests whether concat fusion with avgpool could unexpectedly close the gap to transformer-based configs. Rationale: With 1 experiment left after this one, this is the most informative remaining test—it confirms the aggregation hierarchy and rules out any hidden synergy between avgpool and concat before we lock in config_049 as the final best. Expected cost: moderate (~4–5 GPU hours, similar to config_019's 4.82), slightly higher than config_049's 3.60 due to concat fusion overhead, but acceptable given the confirmation value.

The top-4 results (all scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile) span 0.706–0.725, and all four aggregation×fusion combinations for that pairing have been tested, with config_049 (transformer + weighted) at 0.7250 as the current best. No untested configuration is likely to substantially exceed this, but config_047 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) is the most logical exploitation step: it retains the best RNA encoder (scvi_n200, clearly superior to scgpt and pca_n2000) and the best aggregation/fusion pairing (transformer + weighted), testing only the image encoder swap. While imagenet_vit_l has been consistently stronger, the transformer aggregation may interact differently with a lighter backbone, and this is the highest-expected-accuracy untested option. Expected cost is moderate-to-low (~2.5–3.5 GPU hours), cheaper than config_049's 3.60 h since ResNet-50 is a smaller encoder than ViT-L, keeping total budget manageable. As the final experiment, it represents the best remaining chance to match or marginally exceed 0.7250 while confirming whether the transformer-aggregation advantage is encoder-agnostic.

With no prior evidence, the most important uncertainty is whether the multimodal pipeline (RNA + image) provides a meaningful accuracy gain over unimodal baselines, and which core components form a strong foundation. config_011 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) directly tests this core hypothesis using well-established, moderate-cost components: scvi_n200 is a learned single-cell encoder likely superior to PCA for capturing biological variance; resnet50 is a proven image backbone that is cheaper than ViT-L; transformer aggregation is the most expressive pooling for multiprofile data; and concat fusion is the simplest baseline fusion strategy. This gives a strong reference point for the multimodal direction while avoiding the highest-cost ViT-L encoder. Expected relative cost: medium-high (roughly 3–4× a single-profile RNA-only baseline due to dual-modality processing and transformer aggregation over multiple profiles, but notably cheaper than ViT-L-based multimodal configs). Establishing this performance anchor in experiment 1 will efficiently guide the remaining 9 experiments toward the most promising encoder, aggregation, and fusion variants.

Evidence: config_011 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat, multimodal/multiprofile) achieved 0.688 accuracy at 5.16 GPU hours, establishing a baseline for the multimodal multiprofile pipeline.
