The most uncertain and high-impact design choice remaining is the image encoder: ResNet50 is a relatively modest feature extractor compared to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L, which typically provides substantially richer visual representations. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder from ResNet50 to imagenet_vit_l (while holding all other hyperparameters identical) meaningfully improve validation accuracy? This is a clean single-variable A/B test against config_011, so any accuracy delta can be attributed to the image encoder. Rationale: With 8 experiments remaining, investing in the most likely source of a meaningful accuracy gain now is the best use of the next slot. A stronger image encoder is the highest-leverage architectural upgrade available. Expected relative cost: ViT-L has ~2-3× the parameters of ResNet50, so I estimate ~7-9 GPU hours (roughly 1.5× the cost of config_011). This is a justified premium given the potential accuracy lift, and the total budget still leaves room for 7 further experiments.

Evidence: config_021 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat, multiprofile) is the current best at 0.7207 acc, outperforming config_011 (same but resnet50) by 3.3%. Both used concat fusion, so the effect of fusion strategy is untested. Question: Does weighted fusion improve over concat for integrating the two modalities while keeping the same encoders and transformer aggregation? This is a clean single-variable ablation from the best config. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, testing the fusion mechanism first is the highest-information next step because it directly affects how the two strong modalities (scvi_n200 + ViT-L) are combined, and the result will inform whether to explore weighted-fusion variants (e.g., with scgpt or pca) in later experiments. Expected cost: ~4.7 GPU hours, essentially identical to config_021 since only the fusion head changes, making this a low-cost, high-information experiment.

Evidence: All three completed experiments confirm that multimodal + multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l is the strongest family (best: config_006 at 0.7250 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion). The only untested dimension within this best-known setting is the aggregation method (avgpool vs. transformer). Question: Does avgpool aggregation match or exceed transformer aggregation when paired with the best image encoder and weighted fusion? Why this experiment: It directly exploits the strongest evidence while resolving a key design uncertainty. If avgpool performs comparably (~0.72+), it is substantially cheaper than transformer (estimated ~2.5–3.0 GPU hours vs. 3.6–5.2 for transformer), saving budget for later exploration of RNA encoders (scgpt, pca_n2000). If it underperforms, we confirm transformer is necessary and can focus remaining budget on other axes. This is the highest-information, lowest-cost next step given 6 experiments remain.

Evidence: All four completed experiments use scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder. The best configuration (config_006: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) achieves 0.7250 accuracy at only 3.60 GPU hours, and the image encoder (ViT-L >> ResNet50), aggregation (transformer > avgpool), and fusion (weighted ≥ concat) are now well-characterized. The main untested variable that could push accuracy higher is the RNA encoder itself. Question: Does replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a deep generative model for single-cell RNA) while keeping all other components at their best-performing settings (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) yield a meaningful accuracy gain? This is the cleanest single-variable ablation on the most impactful remaining design choice. Why this experiment: With 5 experiments left, testing the RNA encoder under the already-validated best pipeline is the highest-information experiment. If scgpt improves accuracy, it opens a new exploitation direction; if not, it confirms scvi_n200 is sufficient and we can focus remaining budget on profile setting or fine-tuning. Expected cost: ~4–5 GPU hours (scgpt is comparable in training cost to scvi_n200, and the ViT-L + transformer pipeline was ~3.6–4.7 h in prior runs), so it is moderate and well within budget.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_006 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.7250 acc / 0.6847 F1. We have strong evidence that scvi_n200 >> scgpt, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, transformer > avgpool, and weighted ≥ concat. However, the profile_setting dimension (multiprofile vs singleprofile) is completely untested—all 5 completed experiments are multiprofile. Question: Does the multiprofile transformer aggregation genuinely add value over a simpler single-profile multimodal model, or is the added complexity not translating to accuracy gains? config_013 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) pairs the proven-best RNA and image encoders with the preferred weighted fusion but removes the aggregation step entirely. This is the highest-information experiment because it resolves a fundamental architectural question: if singleprofile is competitive, we simplify the pipeline and save GPU hours; if it is clearly worse, we confirm multiprofile aggregation is essential and can focus remaining budget on multiprofile refinements (e.g., pca_n2000 RNA encoder in config_042). Expected cost: moderate-to-low (~2.5–3.5 GPU hours), since singleprofile eliminates the transformer aggregation over multiple profiles, making it cheaper than config_006 (3.60 hrs) while still using the large ViT-L image encoder.

Evidence: config_006 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the best at 0.7250 acc / 0.6847 F1. scgpt is clearly inferior (0.52), resnet50 is inferior to imagenet_vit_l, and avgpool is inferior to transformer. The only major untested dimension in the top-performing regime is the RNA encoder: pca_n2000 (2000-dim linear) vs scvi_n200 (200-dim learned). config_042 pairs pca_n2000 with the proven-best image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted), directly testing whether a higher-dimensional linear RNA representation can match or exceed the learned scvi embedding. This is the highest-value exploration remaining: it either finds a new best or confirms scvi_n200 is optimal, reducing uncertainty for the final 3 experiments. Expected cost is moderate (~3–4 GPU hours), similar to config_006's 3.60 hrs, since PCA encoding is cheap and the ViT-L + transformer pipeline dominates training time.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the best-performing family, with config_006 (transformer, weighted) leading at 0.7250 accuracy. The only untested combination within this family is config_045 (avgpool, concat). Testing it completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the top family, confirming that transformer+weighted is indeed the optimal pairing and ruling out any unexpected interaction. Given that avgpool underperformed transformer (config_046: 0.7062) and concat underperformed weighted (config_021: 0.7207 vs config_006: 0.7250), config_045 is unlikely to beat config_006, but it is the cheapest remaining experiment in the best family (~4–5 GPU hours, similar to config_046's 4.82) and provides definitive closure on the top architecture before spending the final 2 experiments on lower-priority directions. This is the best use of experiment 8 because it reduces residual uncertainty about the optimum at minimal cost, leaving the last 2 slots for any remaining exploration if needed.

All four aggregation×fusion combinations for the top architecture (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile) have been tested, with config_006 (transformer, weighted) as the clear best at 0.725. The evidence strongly indicates scgpt (~0.52) and pca_n2000 (~0.59) are inferior RNA encoders, and resnet50 underperforms imagenet_vit_l (0.688 vs 0.721 for the same aggregation/fusion). Config_038 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) is the closest untested variant to the current best, differing only in image encoder. It tests whether the transformer+weighted fusion advantage is robust to a weaker image encoder, confirming the architecture ranking. I expect accuracy around 0.69–0.70, unlikely to beat config_006, but it is the most informative remaining test given the near-exhausted promising space. Expected cost is ~5 GPU hours (similar to config_011 at 5.16), making it moderately expensive but justified as the final confirmation before the last experiment slot.

Evidence: The best configuration found is config_006 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.7250 acc, 3.60 GPU hrs). All four aggregation×fusion combinations with this top encoder pair have been tested. The next-best encoder pair (scvi_n200 + resnet50) has been tested with transformer+weighted (0.7131) and transformer+concat (0.6878), but the avgpool+weighted combination remains untested. This experiment tests whether the weighted-fusion advantage (consistent across all other pairings) holds with avgpool aggregation and resnet50, completing the systematic exploration of the scvi_n200 multiprofile multimodal space. It is the best use of the final experiment because: (1) it fills the last logical gap in the most promising architecture family, (2) it is relatively cheap (avgpool + resnet50 expected ~4.0–4.5 GPU hrs, comparable to config_046's 4.82 hrs), and (3) while unlikely to surpass 0.7250, it provides confirmation that config_006 is the optimal choice and rules out a cheaper near-equivalent, solidifying the final recommendation with minimal additional cost.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment must establish a strong multimodal baseline and reduce uncertainty about whether combining RNA and image modalities is beneficial. config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the cleanest 'strong default' multimodal setup: it pairs the most powerful image encoder (ViT-L) with a simple, reliable RNA encoder (PCA-2000) and the simplest aggregation/fusion (avgpool + concat), isolating the core question of whether multimodal fusion helps. If this performs well, it sets a high bar and I can then probe which component (encoder, aggregation, fusion) drives the gain. If it underperforms, I know the issue lies in the basic pipeline rather than in complex choices. Cost: moderate-to-high due to ViT-L and multiprofile processing, but this is justified as the anchor experiment for the entire search. A cheaper alternative (ResNet50) would save GPU hours but risks underestimating the image modality's contribution, making downstream comparisons less informative.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ViT-L, avgpool, concat → 62.9% acc, 4.54 GPU hrs), the most critical uncertainty is whether the RNA modality actually adds meaningful value over image-only. Config_009 (image_only, multiprofile, ViT-L, avgpool) is a clean ablation that removes only the RNA branch while keeping the image encoder (ViT-L), profile setting (multiprofile), and aggregation (avgpool) identical to config_001. If image-only approaches ~62%, we can redirect remaining budget toward cheaper image-centric or single-modality configurations. If it falls well below, multimodal fusion is confirmed essential and we should invest in stronger RNA encoders (scGPT, scVI) and fusion strategies. Expected relative cost: moderate (~3–3.5 GPU hrs), cheaper than config_001 since there is no RNA encoding or cross-modal fusion, but still uses the expensive ViT-L backbone. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the core architectural choice (multimodal vs. unimodal) before committing remaining budget to specific encoder/fusion variants.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieved 62.9% acc, while image-only config_009 (imagenet_vit_l) reached only 33.2%. This ~30-point gap shows RNA is the dominant modality, making the RNA encoder the highest-leverage design choice. Question: Does upgrading the RNA encoder from a linear PCA projection (pca_n2000) to a learned, context-aware transformer (scgpt) improve accuracy while keeping all other settings identical to the current best? config_050 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) isolates exactly this single variable, providing a clean comparison against config_001. Why this is the best next experiment: With 7 experiments remaining, establishing whether a learned RNA encoder helps (or hurts) is the most uncertainty-reducing step. If scgpt improves accuracy, subsequent experiments can explore scgpt combined with transformer aggregation or weighted fusion. If it does not, we confirm PCA suffices and pivot to aggregation/fusion changes. Expected cost: scgpt is a pretrained transformer encoder (heavier than PCA), so I estimate ~5.5–6.5 GPU hours, modestly more expensive than config_001's 4.54 hrs but well within remaining budget.

Evidence: config_001 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the best at 0.629 acc, while config_050 (scgpt variant) underperforms at 0.518 and costs more, confirming pca_n2000 is the superior RNA encoder. config_009 (image-only) at 0.332 confirms multimodal is essential. The remaining uncertainty is whether the fusion mechanism (concat vs weighted) meaningfully affects performance. This experiment tests weighted fusion as the sole change from the best config, directly clarifying whether learned channel weighting improves over simple concatenation. It is the best use of this slot because it is a minimal, single-variable perturbation of the top performer with expected cost similar to config_001 (~4.5 GPU hours, since weighted fusion is a lightweight learned scalar per modality rather than a new module), making it the cheapest informative step. A positive result opens a family of weighted-fusion configs to exploit; a null result lets us redirect budget toward aggregation (transformer) or image-encoder ablations without wasting a slot.

Evidence: The current best (config_020: pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.6352 acc / 0.6183 F1 at 7.02 GPU hrs. PCA clearly outperforms scgpt (0.629 vs 0.518), and weighted fusion slightly edges out concat. The major untested dimension with the best-known settings is the profile aggregation method (avgpool vs transformer). Question: config_022 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a single-variable change from the current best, testing whether transformer-based aggregation across multiple profiles captures inter-profile interactions that simple average pooling misses. This is the highest-uncertainty, highest-potential-impact knob remaining. Rationale: With 5 experiments left after this one, exploiting the proven backbone (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted) while probing the one untested structural change (transformer aggregation) is the most efficient path to either confirm avgpool suffices or discover a meaningful accuracy gain. Expected cost: transformer aggregation adds self-attention layers over profiles, so I estimate ~8–10 GPU hrs (moderately higher than the 7.02 for avgpool+weighted), which is acceptable given its potential to unlock the best configuration.

Evidence: The current best (config_020, acc=0.6352) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. We've confirmed that multimodal >> image_only, avgpool > transformer, weighted ≥ concat, and pca_n2000 > scgpt (0.6287 vs 0.5176). The main untested dimension within the proven-best architecture is the RNA encoder: scvi_n2000 (a learned variational representation) has not been paired with the winning image encoder, aggregation, and fusion settings. This experiment tests whether scvi_n2000 can surpass pca_n2000 by capturing richer biological structure while keeping all other settings at their empirically best values. It is the best use of this slot because it directly extends the strongest configuration along the most impactful untested axis (RNA representation quality), and a positive result would immediately give a new best; a negative result confirms pca_n2000 is optimal and narrows the remaining 4 experiments to image-encoder or profile-setting variations. Expected relative cost: moderate (~6–7 GPU hours), comparable to config_020 (7.02) since it uses the same ViT-L backbone and weighted fusion, with scvi_n2000 likely similar in training overhead to scgpt.

Evidence: config_007 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) is the clear best at 0.706 acc, far ahead of the runner-up config_020 (pca_n2000, avgpool, weighted) at 0.635. With pca_n2000, transformer aggregation was worse than avgpool (0.586 vs 0.635), but scvi_n200 produces a learned, structured latent representation that may interact differently with attention-based aggregation than a linear PCA projection. Question: Does transformer aggregation unlock additional gains when paired with the stronger scvi_n200 encoder, potentially pushing accuracy above 0.706? This is the single most informative untested extension of the current best configuration—changing only the aggregation while keeping the proven best RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion. Why this experiment: It directly exploits the strongest evidence (scvi_n200 + weighted fusion) while resolving the key remaining uncertainty about aggregation. If it beats 0.706, we have a new best; if not, it confirms avgpool is optimal and frees remaining budget for other directions (e.g., singleprofile or resnet50). Expected cost: moderate, roughly 5–6 GPU hours (transformer aggregation adds attention overhead over avgpool, but scvi_n200 is lighter than scgpt), well within the remaining budget of ~3 experiments.

The current best is config_015 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy / 0.6847 F1. The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer as the top-performing architecture, with weighted fusion at 0.7250 vs avgpool at 0.7062. The one untested cell in this top combination is concat fusion with transformer aggregation (config_033). While weighted has outperformed concat in prior comparisons (pca_n2000: 0.6352 vs 0.6287; scvi_n200 avgpool: 0.7062 vs untested), the interaction between transformer aggregation and concat fusion is unknown—concat preserves full representation and may complement transformer's attention-based aggregation differently than weighted does. This experiment directly tests whether a small architectural tweak to the best config can push accuracy above 0.7250. Expected cost is comparable to config_015 (~3.5–3.6 GPU hours) since the architecture is identical except for the fusion method (concat is marginally cheaper than weighted as it avoids learning per-modality weights). With 2 experiments remaining after this, confirming or ruling out concat fusion here preserves the final experiment for a more exploratory direction if needed.

The current best is config_015 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the optimal encoder pair, and transformer aggregation as superior to avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706). The remaining untested multiprofile multimodal config with this encoder pair is config_034 (avgpool, concat). Testing it completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the best encoders, clarifying whether the small transformer-over-avgpool gap holds for the concat fusion variant as well. This is the highest-probability candidate to approach or marginally exceed 0.725 among all remaining options, since it retains both proven encoders. It also informs the final experiment: if config_034 lands near 0.72, the remaining slot is better spent exploring resnet50 variants (e.g., config_039) for cost efficiency; if it lands closer to 0.725, it confirms robustness. Expected cost is moderate (~4.5–5 GPU hours), comparable to config_007 (4.82 h) since it uses avgpool rather than transformer aggregation with the same encoder pair.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_015 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) at 0.725 accuracy, with config_033 (transformer+concat, 0.721) and config_034 (avgpool+concat, 0.715) close behind. This clearly establishes scvi_n200 as the superior RNA encoder and transformer+weighted as the best aggregation/fusion pairing. All scvi_n200 + ViT-L + multiprofile combinations are now tested. Question: This experiment tests whether the best aggregation strategy (transformer + weighted) transfers to ResNet50 as the image encoder, completing the design-space picture for the top RNA encoder. It also reveals whether a cheaper image backbone could approach ViT-L's performance with this aggregation. Rationale: As the final experiment, this is the most informative remaining test—it pairs the two best-validated components (scvi_n200, transformer+weighted) with the only untested image encoder in the multiprofile setting, confirming whether ViT-L is essential or whether ResNet50 offers a cost-effective near-equivalent. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-low (~2.5–3.5 GPU hours), since ResNet50 is a smaller backbone than ViT-L, making this cheaper than config_015 (3.60 hrs) while still providing a definitive answer on the image-encoder axis.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment must establish a performance baseline for the multimodal approach while keeping costs low to preserve budget for exploration. Config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) tests the core hypothesis that combining RNA and image modalities improves accuracy, and simultaneously probes whether multiprofile aggregation with simple avgpool pooling is beneficial. It uses the cheapest image encoder (ResNet50 vs. ViT-L), a linear RNA encoder (PCA), and simple fusion (concat), making it a low-cost experiment (expected relative cost: low, roughly 1x baseline GPU hours). This gives me a reference accuracy to compare against more expensive variants (better encoders, transformer aggregation, ViT-L) in subsequent experiments. If it performs well, I can exploit by upgrading components; if poorly, I learn that the multimodal design space needs different structural choices, reducing uncertainty about which dimensions matter most.

With only one completed experiment (config_009: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat → 61.9% acc, 36.42 GPU hrs), evidence is extremely sparse. The most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually adding value over the image modality alone. Config_003 (image_only, multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool) is a clean ablation of config_009 that removes only the RNA branch while keeping the same image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation. This directly tests whether the ~62% accuracy is driven by the image features or genuinely benefits from RNA fusion. If image_only approaches 62%, we know RNA adds little and should invest in better image encoders; if it drops substantially, multimodal fusion is confirmed as the right direction and we should explore better RNA encoders and fusion strategies. Expected cost is moderate-to-low (~20-25 GPU hrs) since it omits RNA processing entirely, making it a cheap and high-information experiment that preserves budget for later exploitation.

Evidence: config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieved 0.619 accuracy, far exceeding image_only config_003 (0.328), confirming RNA is critical. The image modality alone contributed ~0.33, suggesting the image encoder has room to improve. Question: config_015 is a clean single-variable ablation of config_009, swapping resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings identical (pca_n2000, avgpool, concat, multiprofile). This isolates whether a stronger image backbone (ViT-L vs ResNet50) yields meaningful accuracy gains. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, establishing whether the image encoder is a bottleneck is high-value; if ViT-L helps, subsequent experiments can combine it with better RNA encoders (scgpt/scvi_n200) and transformer aggregation. If it does not, we can focus budget on RNA-side improvements. Expected cost: ViT-L is a larger backbone than ResNet50, so I estimate ~45–55 GPU hours (roughly 1.3–1.5× config_009's 36.42 h), which is acceptable given the potential accuracy gain and the remaining budget.

Evidence: config_015 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the best performer so far at 0.6287 accuracy with very low cost (4.54 GPU hrs), slightly beating config_009 (resnet50, concat) at 0.6186. Image-only is clearly inferior (0.3275), confirming multimodal is essential. Question: config_005 is the direct extension of config_015 with only the fusion strategy changed from concat to weighted. This tests whether learning a weighted combination of modalities (rather than simple concatenation) can further improve accuracy, which is a fundamental design choice in multimodal fusion. Rationale: This is the cheapest and most interpretable next step—same architecture, same encoders, same aggregation—so any accuracy difference is attributable to the fusion mechanism. Expected cost is similar to config_015 (~4-5 GPU hrs), making it very affordable. If weighted fusion helps, it establishes a direction for combining with other improvements (e.g., transformer aggregation, different RNA encoders) in subsequent experiments. If it does not, we confirm concat is sufficient and can pivot to testing RNA encoder or aggregation changes with the remaining budget.

Evidence: The current best (config_005, acc=0.6352) uses pca_n2000 (a simple linear projection) as the RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l and weighted fusion. Image-only baselines confirm multimodal is essential, and ViT-L + weighted fusion is the best image/fusion combo found. The largest unexplored axis is the RNA encoder: we have only tested PCA, while scvi_n200 learns a nonlinear latent representation that may capture richer biological signal. This experiment (config_048: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) isolates the RNA-encoder effect by keeping the best image encoder, aggregation, and fusion from config_005 unchanged. If it improves, it validates investing in learned RNA encoders for subsequent experiments; if not, it redirects focus toward aggregation (transformer) or other factors. Expected cost is moderate (~5–8 GPU hrs), comparable to config_005, since scvi_n200 is a compact 200-dim model and the image/aggregation pipeline is identical to the 7.02-GPU-hr config_005. With 5 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information, cost-efficient next step.

Evidence: config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, multiprofile) is the clear best at 0.7062 acc / 0.6671 F1, a ~7-point jump over the next-best (config_005 at 0.6352) driven primarily by the scvi_n200 RNA encoder. Weighted fusion also consistently beats concat (config_005 vs config_015). The one untested dimension within this top-performing recipe is the aggregation strategy: config_048 uses avgpool, which treats all profiles symmetrically and discards inter-profile structure. Question: config_029 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) tests whether a transformer over the multiprofile sequence can capture profile-level interactions that avgpool misses, while keeping every other setting at its proven optimum. Why this is the best next experiment: it is the single most informative exploitation step—only one variable changes from the current best, so any gain or loss is cleanly attributable to aggregation. With 4 experiments left, resolving this question early lets the remaining budget focus on fine-tuning or confirming the winner. Expected relative cost: transformer aggregation over multiple profiles adds attention overhead, so I estimate roughly 10–15 GPU hours (moderately higher than config_048's 4.82 but well below config_009's 36.42), which is acceptable given the high expected accuracy payoff.

Evidence: The best config (config_029, acc=0.7250) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The progression from pca_n2000→scvi_n200 (+0.07) and avgpool→transformer (+0.019) shows clear gains from better RNA encoding and aggregation. The key unexplored dimension is whether scgpt (a more expressive generative RNA encoder) can surpass scvi_n200 in this optimal architecture. This experiment (config_042: scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) directly tests that hypothesis. It is the highest-value exploration because scgpt is the only RNA encoder not yet paired with the best image encoder + aggregation + fusion combination, and a positive result would open a new optimization axis. Cost: scgpt is a larger model than scvi_n200, but imagenet_vit_l and transformer aggregation are cheap; expected cost is moderate (~5-8 GPU hours), well within budget given 77.21 already spent and 3 experiments remaining. This is the best use of experiment 7 because it targets the largest remaining source of potential improvement while staying in the proven high-performing region of the search space.

The current best is config_029 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. The evidence strongly supports this architecture: scvi_n200 >> pca_n2000 (~7% gain), imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, transformer > avgpool (~2% gain), and weighted > concat (small but consistent). The one remaining untested variant of this top architecture is config_007, which swaps fusion from weighted to concat while keeping transformer aggregation. This directly tests whether the fusion choice still matters under transformer aggregation (where the two modality representations are already being mixed by attention). If concat performs comparably, it confirms config_029 is near-optimal and we can lock in the best config with 2 experiments remaining for potential fine-tuning. If concat unexpectedly outperforms, we gain a new best. Expected cost is similar to config_029 (~3.5–4 GPU hours), keeping total well within budget and leaving room for 2 more experiments.

The current best is config_029 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.7250 acc) with config_007 (same but concat fusion, 0.7207) very close. The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the optimal encoder pair, with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion as the best aggregation/fusion choices. Config_010 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) is the one remaining cell in the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for this encoder pair, completing the design-space evidence. While it is unlikely to surpass config_029 (avgpool underperformed transformer by ~0.02 in config_048 vs 029, and concat underperformed weighted by ~0.004 in config_007 vs 029), it is the most informative and cheapest remaining experiment (~4–5 GPU hours, comparable to config_048's 4.82 hrs) in the primary design space. Running it now leaves the final experiment free to either exploit a surprise or perform a targeted confirmation, making this the best use of experiment 9 under the 1-experiment-remaining constraint.

Evidence: The top 4 performers all use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile, with config_029 (transformer+weighted) leading at 0.7250. All four aggregation×fusion combinations for this encoder pair have been tested, so no further gains are expected within that sub-space. The remaining untested scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l configs (034, 036) are singleprofile variants that remove the aggregation step. Question: This experiment tests whether the multiprofile aggregation step is truly necessary or whether a single profile with the strong scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l encoders and weighted fusion can approach the multiprofile results. Rationale: As the final experiment, the primary goal is to confirm the best result (0.7250) is robust and to minimize total GPU cost. config_036 uses the best-performing RNA and image encoders with weighted fusion (slightly favored in the evidence), and as a singleprofile model with no aggregation layer, it is expected to be the cheapest remaining option (~2-3 GPU hours vs. 3-5 for multiprofile+transformer configs). While it is unlikely to surpass 0.7250, it is the most cost-effective use of the last slot and provides a useful lower-bound on the contribution of multiprofile aggregation.

With no prior evidence, the primary uncertainty is whether a multimodal setup (combining RNA and image features) outperforms unimodal baselines, and which moderate-complexity architecture serves as a strong starting point. config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) tests the core hypothesis that fusing a learned 200-dim RNA latent (scvi_n200) with a standard CNN image embedding (resnet50) via weighted fusion, with simple average-pool aggregation across multiple profiles, yields strong validation accuracy. It avoids the most expensive choices (ViT-L, transformer aggregation) while still being a fully multimodal, multiprofile pipeline. This gives a solid performance anchor at moderate cost (estimated ~2-3x the cost of a single-modality resnet50 config, well below ViT-L + transformer configs), leaving budget for 9 further experiments to explore whether upgrading the image encoder, switching to transformer aggregation, or changing the RNA encoder yields meaningful gains.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.678 accuracy at 5.90 GPU hours, establishing a baseline. With only one data point, the largest single architectural lever for improving accuracy is the image encoder quality — resnet50 (~25M params) is substantially weaker than imagenet_vit_l (~307M params), and in multimodal cellular profiling the image modality often carries critical morphological features. Question tested: Does upgrading the image encoder from resnet50 to ViT-L (while holding all other config_018 settings constant) meaningfully improve validation accuracy? This is a clean one-variable comparison that isolates the image encoder's contribution. Why this is the best next experiment: It has the highest expected accuracy gain of any single change available, and if it succeeds, it validates a large family of ViT-L-based configurations (config_008, 022, 029, 032, etc.) for subsequent exploitation. If it does not help, it tells me the bottleneck is elsewhere (RNA encoder, aggregation, fusion) and I can redirect. Expected relative cost: ViT-L is roughly 3–4× the parameter count of resnet50, so I estimate ~9–12 GPU hours (moderately more expensive than config_018's 5.90), but well within the remaining budget for 8 experiments.

Evidence: config_005 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, multiprofile) achieved the best accuracy (0.7062) at a lower cost (4.82 GPU hrs) than config_018 (resnet50 variant, 0.6776, 5.90 GPU hrs), strongly indicating imagenet_vit_l is the superior image encoder. Uncertainty: whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool by modeling inter-profile interactions in the multiprofile setting. This experiment (config_032) tests exactly that: it is identical to config_005 except avgpool→transformer, isolating the aggregation variable. If transformer aggregation helps, it could push accuracy above 0.71; if not, we confirm avgpool suffices and can pivot to other levers (RNA encoder, profile setting). This is the highest-value single-variable extension of the current best configuration. Expected cost: moderate increase over config_005 (~5.5–6.5 GPU hrs) due to the transformer aggregation layers, but still well within budget with 7 experiments remaining.

The three completed experiments all used scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, so the RNA encoder choice is the largest unexplored design axis. Evidence: The top-3 experiments (config_018→005→032) show a clear progression driven by image encoder (resnet50→imagenet_vit_l, +2.9pp) and aggregation (avgpool→transformer, +1.9pp), with scvi_n200 consistently outperforming scgpt (0.725 vs 0.520). Expected cost: comparable to config_032 (~3.5–4.0 GPU hours), since the architecture is identical except for the fusion operation, making it a moderate-cost experiment relative to the resnet50-based configs (~5.9h).

Evidence: The top-3 configs (config_032: 0.7250, config_029: 0.7207, config_005: 0.7062) all use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, confirming these as strong choices. Transformer aggregation clearly outperforms avgpool (+0.019), and weighted vs concat fusion is nearly equivalent (0.004 gap). However, pca_n2000 as an RNA encoder has never been tested in any multimodal setup, leaving a key uncertainty: whether a simpler, cheaper linear projection can match the learned VAE (scvi_n200). If pca_n2000 is competitive, it offers a significantly cheaper alternative (PCA is a linear projection vs. a multi-step VAE training), reducing GPU cost. If it underperforms, we confirm scvi_n200 is essential and can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning around the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer core. Expected relative cost: slightly lower than config_032 (3.60 GPU hrs), estimated ~2.5–3.5 GPU hours, since PCA encoding is far cheaper than scvi training while the ViT-L and transformer aggregation costs remain similar.

The current best (config_032, 0.7250) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation + weighted fusion in a multiprofile setting. All component-level comparisons (RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation, fusion) have been explored within multiprofile, and the remaining untested multiprofile variants (e.g., config_014 with resnet50, config_051 with avgpool+concat) are unlikely to exceed 0.725 given the clear evidence that imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 and transformer > avgpool. If it is competitive, it would also be cheaper (no aggregation step, estimated ~3–4 GPU hours vs. 3.6–5.9 for multiprofile counterparts), leaving more budget headroom. If it is clearly worse, it confirms multiprofile aggregation is essential and we can confidently exploit config_032 in the remaining 3 experiments. This is the highest-information experiment available under the remaining budget.

The current best is config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc 0.725). All four aggregation×fusion combinations for this top family have been tested except avgpool+concat (config_051). Evidence strongly suggests avgpool underperforms transformer (~2% gap: 0.706 vs 0.725) and concat is marginally below weighted (~0.4% gap: 0.721 vs 0.725), so config_051 is unlikely to beat config_032 but completing this cell confirms the full landscape of the best-performing family. The current best is config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725, 3.60 GPU hrs). All four aggregation×fusion combinations for this core architecture have been tested, and alternative RNA encoders (scgpt: 0.52, pca: 0.59) and the singleprofile setting (0.54) are clearly inferior. Given that no untested configuration with the full best architecture remains, this is the most informative test left: it clarifies the image-encoder contribution under the best aggregation/fusion setting and, if it lands near 0.72, could offer a cheaper alternative. Expected relative cost: moderate (~4–5 GPU hours), comparable to config_018 (5.90) but potentially lower given that transformer aggregation was cheaper than avgpool in the imagenet_vit_l setting.

The current best is config_032 (scvi_n200, vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc / 0.685 F1. All top performers share scvi_n200 + transformer aggregation, confirming these as the key design choices. The remaining uncertainty is whether the resnet50 + transformer + concat combination (config_043) with scvi_n200 can approach or exceed config_032, given that config_014 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved the highest F1 (0.6945) of any experiment, suggesting resnet50 may capture complementary features. Config_043 is the closest untested variant to the best configuration, using the best RNA encoder and aggregation while testing the concat fusion alternative with resnet50. Expected cost: ~5.5–6.2 GPU hours (comparable to config_014 at 6.22 hrs, possibly slightly lower with concat fusion), keeping total budget around 43–44 GPU hours.

With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion (RNA + image) provides any signal over simpler baselines. config_009 is the simplest multimodal setup: singleprofile, PCA (n=2000) for RNA, ResNet50 for image, and a basic concat fusion with no aggregation. This directly tests the core hypothesis of the study—does combining modalities help—while using well-established, low-complexity components. Expected relative cost is LOW-MODERATE (PCA is trivial, ResNet50 is standard, no transformer or large ViT, single profile), preserving GPU budget for the remaining 9 experiments. If it performs well, I can escalate to multiprofile, scgpt/scvi encoders, or transformer aggregation in subsequent runs; if it underperforms, it isolates whether the issue is the fusion strategy or the modalities themselves, guiding targeted exploration. Starting with the simplest informative configuration minimizes confounds and maximizes the information gained per GPU hour in this first experiment.

With only one completed experiment (config_009: singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat → 52.7% acc, 0.85 GPU hrs), evidence is extremely sparse. The most impactful architectural uncertainty is whether multiprofile processing (capturing temporal/dynamic cellular information) provides a meaningful boost over singleprofile. config_010 isolates this variable: it keeps the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (resnet50), and fusion (concat) as the baseline, changing only profile_setting to multiprofile with the simplest aggregation (avgpool). This cleanly tests whether multiprofile helps before committing to more expensive aggregation strategies (transformer) or heavier encoders (scgpt, ViT-L). If multiprofile + avgpool shows a clear improvement, subsequent experiments can exploit that direction with transformer aggregation or better encoders. Expected cost: modestly higher than config_009 (~1.3–1.7 GPU hrs) due to processing multiple profiles and avgpool, but still in the cheaper tier compared to ViT-L or transformer-based configs.

Evidence: config_010 (multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieved 0.619 accuracy, a strong ~9% gain over the singleprofile baseline (config_009, 0.527), confirming multiprofile aggregation is critical. The current best uses a relatively modest ResNet50 image encoder. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L (substantially larger capacity, ~300M vs ~25M params) improve multimodal fusion performance while keeping the proven multiprofile + avgpool + concat pipeline intact? This is a clean single-variable change from the current best, isolating the image-encoder effect. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, testing the most impactful single architectural upgrade (image encoder) is the highest-information next step. If ViT-L helps, subsequent experiments can combine it with a learned RNA encoder (scgpt/scvi) for further gains. Expected cost: moderately higher than config_010's 36.42 GPU hours (likely ~50–65 GPU hours) due to the larger ViT-L backbone, but justified by the expected accuracy gain and the fact that it directly extends the strongest configuration found so far.

Evidence: The current best (config_021, acc=0.6287) uses pca_n2000 (a linear dimensionality reduction) for RNA, imagenet_vit_l for images, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion. Multiprofile with ViT_L and avgpool is clearly the winning architecture (config_021 >> config_009, and config_021 slightly beats config_010 while being 8× cheaper). The largest untested lever on the current best is the RNA encoder: scgpt is a learned, biologically-informed transformer representation that should capture nonlinear gene-gene interactions far better than PCA. Question: Does replacing pca_n2000 with scgpt (while keeping the proven ViT_L + avgpool + concat backbone) yield a meaningful accuracy gain? Why this experiment: It is the single most impactful design change to test next, directly extends the current best configuration, and isolates the RNA-encoder variable for clean attribution. Expected relative cost: moderate — scgpt adds transformer-based RNA encoding overhead, but with the cheap ViT_L image encoder the total should be roughly 6–10 GPU hours, well within budget and far less than the 36.42 hrs of config_010. With 6 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information, cost-effective next step.

Evidence: config_021 (multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the current best at 0.629 acc / 0.599 F1 for only 4.54 GPU hrs, and it outperforms both the resnet50 variant (config_010, 0.619) and the scgpt variant (config_013, 0.518). The dominant design choices (multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool) are well-supported. The remaining untested dimension on this exact backbone is the fusion method: concat (tested) vs. weighted (untested). Question: Can learned weighted fusion between the RNA and image branches improve over simple concatenation, potentially closing the small accuracy gap or pushing past 0.63? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a single-variable change from the current best, so any accuracy shift is cleanly attributable to the fusion strategy. Expected cost is comparable to config_021 (~4–5 GPU hrs) since the architecture is identical. With 5 experiments remaining, this cheap, high-information exploitation step either yields a new best or confirms concat suffices, freeing later budget for larger structural changes (e.g., transformer aggregation or scvi_n200).

Evidence: The best result so far is config_002 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, acc=0.6352). Across experiments, multiprofile >> singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, weighted > concat, and pca_n2000 >> scgpt. The one untested axis within this best-performing region is aggregation method: all top configs use avgpool, but transformer aggregation has not been paired with the optimal (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted) combination. Question: Can transformer aggregation capture inter-profile interactions that avgpool misses, pushing accuracy above 0.635? Why this experiment: It is a minimal, logical extension of the current best (changing only aggregation), directly exploiting the strongest evidence while testing the most impactful remaining design choice. Expected cost: transformer aggregation adds moderate overhead over the ~7 GPU hours of config_002, so I estimate ~12–18 GPU hours—well within budget and far cheaper than the resnet50 multiprofile outlier (36.4). With 4 experiments remaining, this balances exploitation of the proven best region against the high-value uncertainty about aggregation architecture.

Evidence: The current best (config_002, 0.6352 acc) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted + multiprofile. Across experiments, multiprofile > singleprofile, vit_l > resnet50, avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat, and pca_n2000 >> scgpt (0.635 vs 0.518). The only untested dimension at the known-best settings is the RNA encoder: scvi_n200. This experiment tests whether a learned VAE-based 200-dim RNA representation can match or exceed PCA-2000 while retaining the strong image and fusion pipeline. It is the highest-value exploration because it is the sole remaining untested axis with all other hyperparameters fixed at their empirically best values; a positive result would yield a new best configuration, while a negative result definitively confirms pca_n2000 as optimal and lets the remaining 2 experiments focus on fine-tuning other aspects. Expected cost is moderate (~7–10 GPU hours), comparable to config_002, since the architecture is identical apart from the RNA encoder (a small 200-dim VAE), keeping total budget well within limits.

The best result so far is config_020 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) at 0.706 accuracy. The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation, which underperformed avgpool for pca_n2000 (0.586 vs 0.635), might interact differently with the richer learned scvi_n200 representations. config_028 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) isolates this single change while keeping all other parameters at their best-known values. If transformer helps, it could push accuracy above 0.706; if not, it confirms avgpool is optimal for scvi_n200 and the remaining budget can target other refinements. Expected cost is moderate (~5-6 GPU hours, comparable to config_047 at 4.55 and config_020 at 4.82), leaving sufficient budget for one more experiment.

The evidence strongly points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer as the best architecture (config_028: 0.7250 acc, 3.60 GPU hrs; config_020: 0.7062 acc). Weighted fusion has consistently outperformed concat across all tested pairings (e.g., 0.7250 vs 0.6287, 0.7062 vs 0.6186), making config_028 the current best. The only untested variant of this top combination is config_008 (same architecture but concat fusion instead of weighted). This experiment tests whether concat fusion could interact differently with transformer aggregation to potentially match or exceed 0.7250. Given that only 1 experiment remains after this one, this is the highest-value test: it either confirms config_028 as the definitive best (if concat underperforms, as expected) or reveals a surprise. Expected cost is very similar to config_028 (~3.5–4.0 GPU hours), since the only difference is the fusion layer (concat vs weighted), making it a cheap confirmation or potential improvement.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer as the best-performing configuration space (config_028: 0.725, config_008: 0.721). The only remaining untested configuration within this proven encoder pair is config_036 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, concat). While the pattern (avgpool+weighted=0.706, transformer+weighted=0.725, transformer+concat=0.721) suggests avgpool+concat will likely land around 0.69–0.71 and not surpass 0.725, it is the closest untested configuration to the proven best and completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion matrix for this encoder pair, reducing residual uncertainty about whether the transformer aggregation gain is robust or partly a fusion-interaction artifact. All other untested options swap to a clearly inferior encoder (resnet50, scgpt) or singleprofile, which showed large performance drops (0.52–0.53). Expected relative cost is moderate (~4–5 GPU hours, comparable to config_020's 4.82 h), since it uses avgpool rather than transformer aggregation. As the final experiment, this is the most informative remaining test within the top-performing design space.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong multimodal baseline while testing the central hypothesis that combining RNA and image modalities outperforms either alone. config_002 (multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion) tests this hypothesis with a learned RNA representation (scvi_n200 captures biological structure better than PCA but is cheaper than scGPT) and a strong pretrained image encoder (ViT-L). Singleprofile avoids aggregation overhead, keeping cost moderate. This configuration sits in the middle of the design space, so the result will be informative in multiple directions: if it performs well, I can explore multiprofile aggregation, scGPT, and concat fusion as extensions; if it underperforms, I can diagnose whether the RNA encoder, image encoder, or fusion strategy is the bottleneck. Expected relative cost: moderate (~60-70% of the most expensive configs like scGPT+ViT-L+transformer aggregation), since scvi_n200 is a lightweight VAE and there is no multiprofile aggregation step, though ViT-L adds significant compute.

With only one completed experiment (config_002: multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion → 53.7% acc, 0.53 GPU hrs), the most important uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation adds meaningful value over a single profile. Config_004 is a clean ablation: it keeps the same RNA encoder (scvi_n200), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and fusion strategy (weighted) but switches to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation. This isolates the effect of profile aggregation. If it improves accuracy, it justifies further investment in multiprofile+transformer variants; if not, it saves budget by ruling out that direction. Expected relative cost: moderate (~0.7–0.9 GPU hrs), slightly higher than config_002 due to processing multiple profiles, but avgpool is cheap compared to transformer aggregation. This is the best use of experiment 2 because it directly extends the current best result along the highest-impact architectural axis while keeping other variables constant.

Evidence: The jump from singleprofile (config_002, acc=0.537) to multiprofile with avgpool (config_004, acc=0.706) shows that multiprofile aggregation is the dominant design factor. The current best (config_004) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted fusion. Question: Can a more expressive aggregation mechanism (transformer vs. avgpool) further improve performance by capturing complex inter-profile interactions? config_012 is a single-variable change from config_004 (avgpool → transformer, keeping everything else identical), making the result cleanly interpretable. Why this is the best next experiment: With 7 experiments remaining, testing the aggregation mechanism is the highest-information single-axis probe. If transformer aggregation helps, it opens a productive direction (transformer + concat, transformer + other encoders); if it does not, we confirm avgpool suffices and can pivot to fusion or encoder variations. Expected relative cost: Transformer aggregation over multiple profiles adds self-attention layers, so I estimate ~6–8 GPU hours (moderately higher than config_004's 4.82), which is acceptable given the high information value and the fact that this is a potentially superior architecture worth the extra compute.

Evidence: The current best is config_012 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.725 acc. The key finding is that multiprofile + transformer aggregation strongly outperforms singleprofile and avgpool. The fusion method (weighted vs. concat) has not yet been tested in the multiprofile + transformer setting. Question: Does concat fusion (which preserves full modality information before a learned projection) outperform weighted fusion (a fixed linear combination) when combined with transformer aggregation? This is a clean single-variable A/B test against config_012, changing only fusion from weighted to concat. Rationale: This is the most direct and informative next step—it exploits the proven architecture (multiprofile, transformer, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) while resolving the one untested design axis. If concat wins, we get a new best; if not, we confirm weighted fusion is optimal and can pivot to RNA/image encoder variations. Expected cost is similar to config_012 (~3.6–3.8 GPU hours), since the architecture is identical except for the fusion head, making this a low-risk, high-information experiment.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_012 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc / 0.685 F1. Key findings: multiprofile >> singleprofile (+0.17 acc), transformer aggregation > avgpool (+0.02 acc), and weighted ≈ concat fusion (negligible difference). The RNA encoder is the major unexplored axis — we have only tested scvi_n200. Question: Does scgpt, a more expressive pretrained single-cell language model, outperform scvi_n200 when paired with the proven best architecture (multiprofile + transformer + weighted + imagenet_vit_l)? This is the highest-value exploration because the RNA encoder directly shapes the modality representation fed into fusion, and scgpt's larger pretrained capacity could capture richer gene-expression semantics. Why this is the best next experiment: It isolates a single variable (RNA encoder) while holding all other settings at their empirically best values, giving a clean comparison to config_012. Expected cost: scgpt is a large transformer-based encoder, so I estimate ~5–6 GPU hours (moderately higher than config_012's 3.60 h due to the larger RNA backbone), which is acceptable given the potential accuracy gain and the 5 remaining experiments.

The current best is config_012 (scvi_n200, vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc 0.725, 3.60 GPU hrs). The largest remaining uncertainty is whether the RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) is driving performance or whether a simpler linear projection suffices. scgpt was catastrophic (0.520), but pca_n2000 is fundamentally different—it's a linear dimensionality reduction, not a generative model. config_030 changes exactly one variable from the best config (scvi_n200 → pca_n2000), making it a clean ablation. If pca_n2000 matches scvi_n200, we get a substantially cheaper pipeline (no generative model training); if it falls short, we confirm scvi_n200's learned latent space is essential and can focus remaining budget on image-encoder or fusion variants. Expected relative cost: moderate, roughly 2–3 GPU hours (PCA encoding is far cheaper than SCVI, while transformer aggregation + ViT-L image processing dominate), making it a cost-efficient probe of a critical design axis with 4 experiments still remaining.

Evidence: The current best (config_012, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. All top-performing configs share the same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and the only other image encoder (resnet50) has not been tested with the best RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and transformer aggregation. The RNA encoder choice has shown to be the dominant factor (scvi_n200 >> pca_n2000 >> scgpt), and aggregation/fusion choices are well-characterized (transformer > avgpool, weighted ≈ concat). Question: Does the image encoder architecture matter when paired with the best RNA encoder and transformer aggregation? Config_019 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) directly isolates this variable. If resnet50 performs comparably (~0.70+), it confirms the image encoder is less critical and saves compute for remaining experiments; if it drops significantly, it validates imagenet_vit_l as essential and focuses remaining budget on other refinements. Expected cost: ResNet50 is smaller than ViT-L, so this should be moderately cheaper than config_012 (3.60 hrs), estimated ~2.5–3.5 GPU hours, making it a cost-effective exploration of the last major untested architectural axis.

The top-performing family is clearly scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation, with config_012 (vit_l, weighted) at 0.725 and config_019 (resnet50, weighted) at 0.713 but the best F1 (0.6945). Config_050 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) is the only remaining untested configuration in this top family. The evidence suggests resnet50 captures complementary image features (best F1 so far) and concat fusion performed nearly identically to weighted with vit_l (0.721 vs 0.725), so combining resnet50's discriminative strength with concat fusion could push accuracy past 0.725. This is a targeted exploitation of the strongest evidence with minimal uncertainty. Expected cost: ~5.5–6.5 GPU hours (similar to config_019's 6.22 h since architecture is nearly identical, only fusion changes from weighted to concat), which is moderate and justified given it is the most likely candidate to set the final best accuracy.

Evidence: The current best (config_012, acc=0.7250) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted in multimodal multiprofile mode. All eight completed experiments strongly confirm that this combination of choices (scvi_n200 > scgpt/pca, multiprofile > singleprofile, transformer > avgpool, weighted ≥ concat, vit_l ≥ resnet50) is optimal. No untested multimodal multiprofile configuration with scvi_n200 offers a plausible path to exceed 0.725; the remaining untested scvi_n200 multimodal configs all involve a step-down (avgpool or resnet50). Question: This experiment tests RNA-only, singleprofile with scvi_n200 to establish a clean, minimal lower bound for the best RNA encoder in isolation, confirming the incremental value of the full multimodal multiprofile pipeline. Why this is the best use: With only 1 experiment remaining after this one, the primary goal shifts to minimizing total GPU cost while the best accuracy is already secured at 0.7250. config_027 requires no image processing, no multiprofile aggregation, and no fusion—making it the cheapest informative experiment (~0.2–0.3 GPU hours vs. 3–6 for multimodal multiprofile configs). It adds a useful reference point at negligible cost, keeping total GPU hours near 32.6 rather than adding 5+ hours for a multimodal run unlikely to improve on the current best.

Evidence: The best configuration found is config_012 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy. All four scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer combinations have been tested, confirming scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l as the top encoders and transformer as the best aggregation. The remaining untested scvi_n200 + multiprofile configs all use avgpool, which underperformed transformer (config_004: 0.7062 vs config_012: 0.7250). Question: config_034 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) is the highest-expected-accuracy untested config, pairing the two best encoders with avgpool and concat fusion. It tests whether concat fusion with the best encoders can narrow the gap to the transformer baseline. Why this is the best last experiment: No untested config is likely to exceed 0.7250 given the strong evidence, but config_034 has the highest ceiling among remaining options since it retains both top encoders. Its expected cost (~4–5 GPU hours, comparable to config_004's 4.82) is moderate, and it provides a useful lower-bound confirmation of the transformer aggregation advantage without the higher cost of resnet50-based alternatives.

With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is whether the full multimodal + multiprofile pipeline is the right direction and how much each component contributes. config_013 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) tests the core hypothesis that combining RNA and image modalities with multi-profile aggregation improves accuracy. It uses a compact learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200, 200-dim) paired with a strong pretrained image encoder (ViT-L), simple average-pool aggregation (cheap baseline before transformer), and standard concat fusion. This establishes a strong reference point: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate components (e.g., drop to singleprofile, swap to resnet50, try transformer aggregation) to understand what drives performance; if it underperforms, I can pivot to simpler or single-modality configurations. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-high (ViT-L is the most expensive image encoder, but avgpool aggregation and the compact 200-dim scvi latent keep the overall training cost manageable compared to transformer-aggregation or scgpt-based configs).

With only one completed experiment (config_013: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, ViT-L, avgpool, concat → 0.715 acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the RNA modality actually adds value over the image modality alone. config_014 (image_only, multiprofile, ViT-L, avgpool) is a clean ablation of config_013 with only the RNA encoder and fusion removed, holding the image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation constant. If config_014 approaches 0.715, the RNA branch is not contributing and we should pivot to optimizing the image pipeline (encoder, aggregation) or try cheaper single-modality configs. If it is substantially lower, multimodal fusion is confirmed as important and we should exploit that direction with different RNA encoders or fusion strategies. This single experiment resolves the highest-impact design question with 8 experiments remaining. Expected cost: moderate (~3–3.5 GPU hours), since it retains the expensive ViT-L image encoder and multiprofile processing but omits the RNA encoder and fusion layers, making it somewhat cheaper than config_013's 4.49 GPU hours.

Evidence: config_013 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieved 0.715 accuracy, far exceeding image-only config_014 (0.332), confirming that multimodal fusion with a learned RNA encoder is the dominant design. The remaining question is whether the simple avgpool aggregation is a bottleneck for combining multiple profiles. This experiment (config_047) isolates that single change—replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping the proven scvi_n200 encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and concat fusion—testing whether learned attention across profiles can outperform uniform averaging. Transformer aggregation is the most architecturally impactful untested dimension for a multiprofile model, as it lets the model weight profiles adaptively rather than treating them equally. Expected cost is moderate: transformer attention adds roughly 1–1.5 GPU hours over the 4.49 h baseline, so ~5.5–6 GPU hours. With 7 experiments remaining, this is a high-value exploitation step on the best-known configuration before branching to other axes (RNA encoder, image encoder, fusion).

Evidence: The two multimodal experiments (config_013: avgpool+concat, acc=0.715; config_047: transformer+concat, acc=0.721) show that aggregation method has negligible impact (~0.006 difference) when using scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + concat fusion. The image-only baseline (0.332) confirms RNA is essential. The key untested variable in the current best setup is the fusion method (weighted vs concat). Question: config_043 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) directly extends the best result (config_047) by swapping concat for weighted fusion, testing whether learned per-modality weighting can further improve accuracy beyond 0.721. Why this is the best next step: With 6 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest evidence (the exact encoder/profile combination that already yields ~0.72) by testing the one untried architectural knob (fusion) is the highest-information, lowest-risk move. It avoids the large uncertainty of switching RNA or image encoders while directly probing whether we can push past the current plateau. Expected cost: ~4.6–4.7 GPU hours, comparable to config_047, since the architecture (same encoders, transformer aggregation) is identical.

Evidence: The best config so far is config_043 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. Across the 2x2 aggregation×fusion grid with scvi_n200, transformer aggregation and weighted fusion both show consistent gains over their alternatives. However, we have only tested one RNA encoder (scvi_n200) in the multimodal multiprofile setting, so the impact of RNA encoder choice remains unexplored. Question: Will scgpt—a more expressive, generative RNA encoder—outperform scvi_n200 when paired with the proven-best aggregation (transformer) and fusion (weighted)? config_037 changes exactly one variable (RNA encoder) from the current best, giving a clean comparison. Why this is the best next experiment: With 5 experiments remaining, identifying whether the RNA encoder is a meaningful lever (or whether scvi_n200 is already near-optimal) is the highest-information test. If scgpt improves accuracy, it opens a promising exploitation path; if not, we can confidently lock in scvi_n200 and focus remaining budget on image-encoder or profile-setting variations. Expected cost: moderate (~4.5–5.5 GPU hours), comparable to config_047, since scgpt is a larger model than scvi_n200 but the overall architecture (transformer aggregation, ViT-L image encoder) is unchanged.

The top-3 configs (043, 047, 013) all use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with multiprofile, and the best (config_043, acc=0.7250) uses transformer aggregation + weighted fusion. The image encoder dimension is completely unexplored with the best RNA/aggregation/fusion settings. config_018 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) tests whether a different visual backbone can match or exceed ViT-L while keeping the proven RNA encoder and fusion strategy. Image-only performance was very low (0.33), so the image branch contributes modestly, but a better/more complementary representation could still push the multimodal accuracy above 0.725. This is the highest-value remaining uncertainty: if resnet50 matches ViT-L, we gain a cheaper pipeline; if it underperforms, we confirm ViT-L is necessary and can focus remaining budget on other refinements. Expected relative cost: lower than config_043 (~2.5–3.0 GPU hrs vs 3.60) since resnet50 is a smaller backbone than ViT-L, making this a cost-efficient exploration of the last major untested architectural axis.

Evidence: The current best is config_043 (scvi_n200, vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. All top-4 results cluster in a narrow 0.713–0.725 band, and the only major untested variable in the best architecture is the RNA encoder type. scgpt was catastrophic (0.52), but pca_n2000 has never been tested in any multimodal setting. Question: Can a simpler linear RNA encoder (pca_n2000) match or exceed scvi_n200 when paired with the best-known aggregation (transformer) and fusion (weighted)? This is critical because if pca_n2000 performs comparably, it is substantially cheaper (no learned RNA model to train), freeing GPU budget for further refinement in the remaining 3 experiments. If it underperforms, we confirm scvi_n200 is the right encoder and can exploit that direction. Rationale: With only 3 experiments left, resolving this uncertainty about the single largest untested architectural choice is the highest-information experiment. Expected cost: ~2.5–3.2 GPU hours (PCA encoding is negligible compared to scvi; the dominant cost is the ViT-L image encoder and transformer fusion, similar to config_043's 3.60 h but without the scvi pre-training overhead), making it a cost-effective probe.

Evidence: The current best is config_043 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. We've tested transformer+weighted (0.725), transformer+concat (0.721), and avgpool+concat (0.715) with the top encoders, but the avgpool+weighted combination remains untested. This experiment tests whether weighted fusion also improves over concat when paired with avgpool aggregation, completing the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the best encoder pair (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l).
